Example::  python tools/download_musan_rirs.py                 # ~200 noise files + 2k RIRs python tools/download_musan_rirs.py --small 0        # full noise subset", "id": "micro/stt-training/tools/download_musan_rirs.py", "kind": "module", "label": "download_musan_rirs.py", "language": "py", "sha256": "d5e53c5509b33b58", "symbol_count": 3, "symbols": [{"kind": "function", "line": 37, "name": "download_musan_noise", "signature": "def download_musan_noise(out_dir, small, seed)"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 67, "name": "download_rirs", "signature": "def download_rirs(out_dir, max_files, seed)"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 94, "name": "main", "signature": "def main()"}]}, {"doc": "Cut per-word training clips from mined People's Speech utterances.  For command rows (data/mined/commands.jsonl) the full utterance is force-aligned with torchaudio's MMS_FA model and one clip is cut around each matched command word. For unknown rows (data/mined/unknown.jsonl) a few random ~1 s windows are cut and labelled ``_unknown_`` (no alignment needed).  Output (Speech-Commands layout, ready for the trainer)::  data/peoples_speech/<label>/ps-<speaker>_nohash_<n>.wav  Runs resume via an ``extracted_keys.jsonl`` sidecar in the output dir.  Requires: ``pip install torch torchaudio soundfile numpy``.  Example::  python tools/extract_clips.py --mined-dir data/mined --output-dir data/peoples_speech", "id": "micro/stt-training/tools/extract_clips.py", "kind": "module", "label": "extract_clips.py", "language": "py", "sha256": "8c4b3c743e360da3", "symbol_count": 11, "symbols": [{"kind": "class", "line": 46, "name": "AlignedWord", "signature": "class AlignedWord"}, {"doc": "Thin wrapper around ``torchaudio.pipelines.MMS_FA`` forced alignment.", "kind": "class", "line": 53, "name": "MMSAligner", "signature": "class MMSAligner"}, {"doc": "Neighbour-clamped clip covering ``[start_s, end_s]`` padded and grown.", "kind": "method", "line": 116, "name": "_cut_natural_clip", "signature": "def _cut_natural_clip(audio, start_s, end_s)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 144, "name": "_resolve_device", "signature": "def _resolve_device(choice)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 156, "name": "_load_rows", "signature": "def _load_rows(path)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 167, "name": "_safe", "signature": "def _safe(s)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 171, "name": "main", "signature": "def main()"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 56, "name": "__init__", "signature": "def __init__(self, device, with_star)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 71, "name": "_ids", "signature": "def _ids(self, word)"}, {"doc": "Return one ``AlignedWord`` per input word (``None`` if unpronounceable).\n\nReturns ``None`` if CTC alignment fails entirely.", "kind": "method", "line": 74, "name": "align", "signature": "def align(self, audio_1d, words)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 212, "name": "emit", "signature": "def emit(label, clip_id, char_start, speaker, clip, sample_rate)"}]}, {"doc": "Mine People's Speech for command words (and generic \"unknown\" speech).  Scans MLCommons/peoples_speech transcripts and, for each utterance that either contains a command word or -- in ``--unknown`` mode -- contains none of them, fetches the audio, resamples it to 16 kHz, and records a JSONL row for the clip extractor to align and cut.  Data source: the Hub's auto-generated Parquet export, read anonymously (no account or token required) over HTTP range requests. We list the shards with ``HfFileSystem`` and read them column-by-column with pyarrow: only the tiny ``text`` column is pulled while scanning, and the (large) ``audio`` column is downloaded only for the row groups that actually contain a hit. This replaces the old ``datasets-server.huggingface.co`` REST API, which is queue-backed and frequently unavailable (HTTP 503).  Two modes: command  (default)  one row per matched command occurrence -> data/mined/commands.jsonl --unknown           one row per non-command utterance      -> data/mined/unknown.jsonl  Output audio cache: ``<mined-dir>/audio/<clip>.wav``. Runs resume: rows already recorded and audio already on disk are skipped.  Requires: ``pip install datasets soundfile`` (pyarrow + huggingface_hub come with ``datasets``).  Example (scan 200k rows of the clean train split for commands)::  python tools/mine_peoples_speech.py --words-file words.txt \\ --split train --limit 200000 --mined-dir data/mined", "id": "micro/stt-training/tools/mine_peoples_speech.py", "kind": "module", "label": "mine_peoples_speech.py", "language": "py", "sha256": "bbeca12d9ad7ba00", "symbol_count": 16, "symbols": [{"kind": "function", "line": 69, "name": "_new_fs", "signature": "def _new_fs()"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 75, "name": "_shard_paths", "signature": "def _shard_paths(config, split)"}, {"doc": "Row-group reader for one Parquet shard, resilient to expiring creds.\n\nAnonymous access to the Hub's Xet/presigned storage uses short-lived\n(~1 h) credentials, so a single long-lived handle 401s partway through a\nbig scan. On any read error we sleep and reopen the shard with a *fresh*\n``HfFileSystem`` (new credentials), which also rides out transient network\nblips. Reopening is cheap: only Parquet metadata is re-fetched.", "kind": "class", "line": 80, "name": "_ShardReader", "signature": "class _ShardReader"}, {"doc": "Yield ``(clip_id, transcript, speaker, fetch_audio)`` rows.\n\nReads the Parquet export anonymously. ``fetch_audio()`` lazily pulls and\ndecodes the audio for its row (downloading that row group's ``audio``\ncolumn only on first use), so scanning stays cheap for non-matching rows.", "kind": "method", "line": 131, "name": "iter_peoples_speech", "signature": "def iter_peoples_speech(config, split, offset, limit)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 187, "name": "_tokens_with_pos", "signature": "def _tokens_with_pos(text)"}, {"doc": "Return ``[(label, char_start, char_end), ...]`` for command words in text.\n\n``targets`` is ``[(label, (tok0, tok1, ...)), ...]`` supporting multi-word\nphrases; all our default commands are single tokens.", "kind": "method", "line": 191, "name": "find_matches", "signature": "def find_matches(text, targets)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 207, "name": "_safe_name", "signature": "def _safe_name(clip_id)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 211, "name": "save_audio_16k", "signature": "def save_audio_16k(fetch, out_path)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 231, "name": "_load_seen_keys", "signature": "def _load_seen_keys(path)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 247, "name": "main", "signature": "def main()"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 90, "name": "__init__", "signature": "def __init__(self, shard, max_attempts)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 98, "name": "_open", "signature": "def _open(self)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 103, "name": "num_row_groups", "signature": "def num_row_groups(self)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 106, "name": "row_group_num_rows", "signature": "def row_group_num_rows(self, rg)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 109, "name": "read_columns", "signature": "def read_columns(self, rg, columns)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 157, "name": "_fetch", "signature": "def _fetch(_rg, _i)"}]}, {"doc": "Synthesize the command vocabulary with Moonshine Voice ZipVoice TTS.  Every word in ``words.txt`` is spoken by each built-in ZipVoice speaker (and, optionally, at a few speeds for prosody variety), resampled to 16 kHz, and written in the Speech-Commands layout the trainer expects::  data/tts/<voice>/<word>/<voice>_nohash_<rep>.wav  The first run downloads the ZipVoice models from the Moonshine CDN (cached under MOONSHINE_VOICE_CACHE). Existing clips are skipped, so runs resume safely.  Requires: ``pip install moonshine-voice librosa soundfile``.  Example::  python tools/synthesize.py --words-file words.txt", "id": "micro/stt-training/tools/synthesize.py", "kind": "module", "label": "synthesize.py", "language": "py", "sha256": "3988732ffa32934e", "symbol_count": 3, "symbols": [{"doc": "Return the installed ZipVoice speakers, falling back to the known list.\n\nQueries moonshine-voice so the voice set tracks whatever the installed\npackage version ships, rather than a hardcoded list that can drift.", "kind": "function", "line": 58, "name": "discover_voices", "signature": "def discover_voices(language)"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 76, "name": "_resample_to_16k", "signature": "def _resample_to_16k(samples, sr)"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 85, "name": "main", "signature": "def main()"}]}, {"doc": "Host (desktop) implementations of the handful of TFLM platform hooks that the modules and the micro_test.h harness reference: the MicroPrintf logging family and tflite::InitializeTarget().  The vendored pico-tflmicro provides these for the RP2350 via system_setup.cpp / debug_log.cpp, both of which call into the Pico SDK and therefore cannot be compiled on the host. For the pure-logic unit tests (feature-generation, the VAD segmenter, the STT predictor, the TTS G2P) we don't need the interpreter at all -- only logging and a no-op init -- so this tiny shim lets those tests build and run on a laptop with a normal compiler.  Interpreter-level tests (real MicroInterpreter inference) are built for the RP2350 target instead, where the full pico-tflmicro library is available.", "id": "micro/test-support/host/tflm_host_stub.cc", "kind": "module", "label": "tflm_host_stub.cc", "language": "cc", "sha256": "8ce1dab63a1a9458", "symbol_count": 5, "symbols": [{"kind": "function", "line": 19, "name": "MicroPrintf", "signature": "void MicroPrintf(const char* format, ...)"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 27, "name": "VMicroPrintf", "signature": "void VMicroPrintf(const char* format, va_list args)"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 32, "name": "MicroSnprintf", "signature": "int MicroSnprintf(char* buffer, size_t buf_size, const char* format, ...)"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 40, "name": "MicroVsnprintf", "signature": "int MicroVsnprintf(char* buffer, size_t buf_size, const char* format,\n                   va_list ..."}, {"kind": "function", "line": 46, "name": "InitializeTarget", "signature": "void InitializeTarget()"}]}, {"doc": "Run a TFLM micro_test.h binary and translate its output into an exit code.  micro_test.h wraps the suite in `while (true) { ... }` (it is designed to run forever on an embedded target and stream results over serial). On the host we read until the first pass/fail banner, then quit -- closing the pipe sends the looping binary a SIGPIPE so it terminates. Exit 0 iff all tests passed.", "id": "micro/test-support/run_micro_test.sh", "kind": "module", "label": "run_micro_test.sh", "language": "sh", "sha256": "0895122590440946", "symbol_count": 0, "symbols": []}, {"doc": "vad -- on-device voice activity detection.  Single public header for the module. It exposes the two halves of the VAD:  * Vad            -- a TFLM wrapper around the int8 TinyVadCNN. Given a normalised (n_mels x window_frames) log-mel window it returns ONE speech probability in [0, 1]. One call per ~32 ms streaming hop.  * VadSegmenter   -- a heap-free moving-average smoother + 1 s clip extractor. It turns the per-frame probabilities into speech-segment boundaries (absolute sample indices on the input stream) without storing any audio.  The streaming log-mel front-end that feeds Vad lives in the feature-generation module (MelStreamer); compose them in your application (see examples/rp2350's audio path). The VAD model is shape-agnostic: the model bytes, arena, and (n_mels, window_frames) are all supplied by the caller, so the module carries no model or platform dependency beyond feature-generation and TFLM.", "id": "micro/vad/include/vad/vad.h", "kind": "module", "label": "vad.h", "language": "h", "sha256": "05bc3f011de8b886", "symbol_count": 19, "symbols": [{"kind": "struct", "line": 38, "name": "VadTensorQuant"}, {"kind": "struct", "line": 72, "name": "Impl"}, {"kind": "enum", "line": 85, "name": "VadEvent"}, {"kind": "class", "line": 43, "name": "Vad"}, {"kind": "class", "line": 85, "name": "VadEvent"}, {"kind": "class", "line": 96, "name": "VadSegmenter"}, {"doc": "Scratch for the fp32 log-mel window, borrowed from the arena overlay (dead until Invoke()). Contract: produce features here, then Predict(it).", "kind": "function", "line": 64, "name": "feature_scratch", "signature": "float* feature_scratch() const"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 66, "name": "input_quant", "signature": "VadTensorQuant input_quant() const"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 67, "name": "output_quant", "signature": "VadTensorQuant output_quant() const"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 68, "name": "input_count", "signature": "std::size_t input_count() const"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 69, "name": "arena_used_bytes", "signature": "std::size_t arena_used_bytes() const"}, {"doc": "Boundaries (absolute sample indices) of the most-recent segment.", "kind": "function", "line": 113, "name": "segment_start_sample", "signature": "std::size_t segment_start_sample() const"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 114, "name": "segment_end_sample", "signature": "std::size_t segment_end_sample() const"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 115, "name": "samples_processed", "signature": "std::size_t samples_processed() const"}, {"doc": "Run one inference on a (n_mels * window_frames) row-major fp32 log-mel window; returns the speech probability in [0, 1] (sigmoid of the dequantized logit). `features` may point at feature_scratch().", "kind": "function", "line": 60, "name": "Predict", "signature": "float Predict(const float* features) const;"}, {"doc": "Reset all state to begin a fresh stream.", "kind": "function", "line": 103, "name": "Start", "signature": "void Start();"}, {"doc": "Front-aligned pad/truncate of src[start, end) into out[0, clip_len): take from the segment start, zero-pad the tail. `out` must hold clip_len floats.", "kind": "function", "line": 135, "name": "ExtractClipFrontAligned", "signature": "void ExtractClipFrontAligned(const float* src, std::size_t src_len, std::size_t start, std::size_t end, float* out, std::size_t clip_len);"}, {"doc": "Power-weighted centroid sample index over buf[start, end): round( sum(i * buf[i]^2) / sum(buf[i]^2) ). Produces, under ``examples/rp2350/generated/``:  vad_config.h          -- audio / front-end / segmenter constants (always). vad_mel_tables.{h,cc} -- precomputed Hann window + CSR Slaney mel filterbank for the VAD front-end (always). vad_model_data.{h,cc} -- the int8 VAD .tflite as a flash byte array (only when a model path is supplied or found under ``models/``). "def finalize_options(self)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 20, "name": "get_tag", "signature": "def get_tag(self)"}]}, {"doc": "Moonshine Voice - Fast, accurate, on-device AI library for building interactive voice applications.  This package provides Python bindings for the Moonshine Voice C API, enabling voice-activity detection, transcription, and other voice processing capabilities.", "id": "python/src/moonshine_voice/__init__.py", "kind": "module", "label": "__init__.py", "language": "py", "sha256": "97f0499d83462eef", "symbol_count": 1, "symbols": [{"doc": "Lazy import for transcriber, mic_transcriber, and intent_recognizer modules.", "kind": "function", "line": 81, "name": "__getattr__", "signature": "def __getattr__(name)"}]}, {"doc": "Alphanumeric listener for character-by-character speech-to-text input.  Designed for dictating passwords, serial numbers, codes, and other alphanumeric strings where the user speaks one character at a time, optionally preceded by modifiers like \"upper case\" or \"capital\".  Usage::  from moonshine_voice import AlphanumericListener  def handle(event): print(event)  listener = AlphanumericListener(handle) transcriber.add_listener(listener)  # User says: \"capital H\", \"e\", \"l\", \"l\", \"o\", \"at sign\", #            \"one\", \"two\", \"three\", \"stop\" # callback receives Character events for H, e, l, l, o, @, 1, 2, 3 # then a Stopped event with text=\"Hello@123\"", "id": "python/src/moonshine_voice/alphanumeric_listener.py", "kind": "module", "label": "alphanumeric_listener.py", "language": "py", "sha256": "bd38b31c8883cd64", "symbol_count": 31, "symbols": [{"kind": "class", "line": 40, "name": "AlphanumericEventType", "signature": "class AlphanumericEventType(Enum)"}, {"doc": "Event delivered to the callback each time something happens.\n\nAttributes\n----------\ntype:\n    The kind of event (CHARACTER, UNDO, CLEAR, or STOPPED).\ncharacter:\n    The resolved character for CHARACTER events, or the removed\n    character for UNDO events. ``None`` for CLEAR / STOPPED.\ntext:\n    The full assembled string *after* this event has been applied.", "kind": "class", "line": 49, "name": "AlphanumericEvent", "signature": "class AlphanumericEvent"}, {"doc": "Pure classification result produced by :class:`AlphanumericMatcher`.\n\nHas a ``type`` (one of :class:`AlphanumericEventType`, with ``NONE``\nmeaning \"unrecognized\") and an optional resolved ``character``.", "kind": "class", "line": 69, "name": "AlphanumericMatch", "signature": "class AlphanumericMatch"}, {"doc": "Return a TTS-friendly phrase for a single character.\n\n* Letters use their spelling-alphabet sounds – ``\"h\"`` → ``\"haitch\"``,\n  ``\"w\"`` → ``\"double you\"``.\n* Upper-case letters are prefixed with ``\"capital \"`` –\n  ``\"H\"`` → ``\"capital haitch\"``.\n* Digits become their word form – ``\"1\"`` → ``\"one\"``.\n* Common symbols use their spoken name – ``\"#\"`` → ``\"hash\"``,\n  ``\"@\"`` → ``\"at sign\"``, ``\" \"`` → ``\"space\"``.\n* Anything else (unknown char, empty string, multi-char input) is\n  returned unchanged so callers never lose information silently.", "kind": "method", "line": 306, "name": "spoken_form", "signature": "def spoken_form(char)"}, {"doc": "Return *text* lower-cased with quotes/punctuation removed.\n\nCharacters in :data:`_NORMALIZE_DROP_CHARS` are deleted, the result is\nlower-cased, and internal runs of whitespace are collapsed to a single\nspace.  Used on both inbound STT text and the vocabulary keys so\nmatching is robust to noisy punctuation while still recognising\nmulti-word phrases like ``\"upper case\"``.", "kind": "method", "line": 355, "name": "_normalize", "signature": "def _normalize(text)"}, {"doc": "Merge all character vocabularies into a single lookup table.", "kind": "method", "line": 370, "name": "_build_lookup", "signature": "def _build_lookup()"}, {"doc": "Parse English number words in the range 10 – 1 000.\n\nHandles forms like:\n  - \"ten\" .. \"nineteen\"\n  - \"twenty\" .. \"ninety nine\" (with or without hyphen)\n  - \"one hundred\" .. \"nine hundred and ninety nine\"\n  - \"a hundred\", \"a thousand\", \"one thousand\"\n\nReturns ``None`` when *text* is not a recognisable number phrase or\nis in the range 0 – 9 (those are handled by the single-digit lookup).", "kind": "method", "line": 424, "name": "_parse_number_words", "signature": "def _parse_number_words(text)"}, {"doc": "Stateless classifier for spelled letter / digit / command utterances.\n\nExposes the \"does this utterance match?\" half of the alphanumeric\nvocabulary as a pure function, without any of the listener or\nbuffer-management machinery.  This is useful for dialog flows that\nwant to reuse the same vocabulary for ``ask(mode=SPELLED)`` or\n``ask(mode=DIGITS)`` prompts without pulling in the whole event\nlistener.\n\nThe same recognition rules apply as for :class:`AlphanumericListener`:\nletters, digits, number words 10-1000, upper-case modifiers, special\ncharacters, and the undo / clear / stop command vocabularies.\n\nParameters\n----------\ncustom_words:\n    Optional dict mapping spoken forms to output characters.  Takes\n    highest priority and overrides built-in mappings.\naccept_letters:\n    If ``False``, utterances that resolve to an alphabetic character\n    are reported as ``NONE`` (useful for digit-only modes).\naccept_digits:\n    If ``False``, utterances that resolve to a digit character are\n    reported as ``NONE`` (useful for letter-only modes).\naccept_specials:\n    If ``False``, utterances that resolve to a special character\n    (``@``, ``#``, …) are reported as ``NONE``.", "kind": "class", "line": 512, "name": "AlphanumericMatcher", "signature": "class AlphanumericMatcher"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 716, "name": "letters_only_matcher", "signature": "def letters_only_matcher()"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 720, "name": "digits_only_matcher", "signature": "def digits_only_matcher()"}, {"doc": "Listens for single-character dictation and assembles the result.\n\nThis is a callable listener — pass it directly to\n``transcriber.add_listener()`` or ``stream.add_listener()``.  It\nreceives raw :class:`TranscriptEvent` objects and internally filters\nfor the events it cares about.  All utterance-level recognition is\ndelegated to :class:`AlphanumericMatcher`; this class only adds the\nlistener plumbing (buffer, undo/clear/stop state, event dispatch).\n\nA single *callback* is invoked every time something meaningful\nhappens.  The callback receives an :class:`AlphanumericEvent` whose\n``type`` field describes what occurred:\n\n* ``CHARACTER`` — a letter, digit, or special character was recognised.\n* ``UNDO``      — the last character was removed.\n* ``CLEAR``     — the buffer was wiped.\n* ``STOPPED``   — the user said \"stop\" / \"done\" / \"finish\" / etc.\n\nSee :class:`AlphanumericMatcher` for the full vocabulary.\n\nParameters\n----------\ncallback:\n    Called on every character, undo, clear, or stop event.\n    Signature: ``(event: AlphanumericEvent) -> None``.\nuse_line_completed:\n    If ``True`` (default), characters are committed on\n    ``LineCompleted`` events (high confidence).  If ``False``,\n    characters are committed on ``LineTextChanged`` for lower\n    latency.\ncustom_words:\n    Optional dict mapping spoken forms to output characters.\n    Takes highest priority and overrides built-in mappings.\nmatcher:\n    Optional pre-built :class:`AlphanumericMatcher`.  When provided,\n    ``custom_words`` is ignored and the matcher is used as-is.\ntts:\n    Optional text-to-speech backend.  When provided:\n\n    * Each ``CHARACTER`` event triggers a ``tts.say(phrase)`` call\n      where ``phrase`` is the output of :func:`spoken_form` (e.g.\n      ``\"haitch\"`` for ``\"h\"``, ``\"capital ay\"`` for ``\"A\"``,\n      ``\"one\"`` for ``\"1\"``, ``\"hash\"`` for ``\"#\"``).\n    * Each utterance the matcher *doesn't* recognise triggers a\n      ``tts.play_error()`` call (a short two-tone beep), so the\n      user hears audible feedback that their last word was\n      ignored instead of waiting in silence.\n\n    The backend needs to expose ``say(text: str) -> None`` for the\n    per-character repeat-back; ``play_error()`` is called only if\n    the backend actually defines it (so simple stubs stay usable).\n    Exceptions from either call are swallowed (and logged under\n    ``debug=True``) so a flaky TTS can't break the listener.\ndebug:\n    If ``True``, unrecognised utterances and TTS errors are logged\n    to stderr.\n\nNotes\n-----\nThe optional spelling-CNN fusion path used to live here as a\nPython ``SpellingPredictor`` + ``FusionStrategy`` smart-router.\nThat logic now ships in the C++ transcriber: build the\n:class:`Transcriber` with ``spelling_model_path=…`` and pass\n``MOONSHINE_FLAG_SPELLING_MODE`` to your ``transcribe_*`` /\n``update_transcription`` calls; this listener will then see\nalready-resolved single-character ``line.text`` values for the\nmatched utterances.", "kind": "class", "line": 738, "name": "AlphanumericListener", "signature": "class AlphanumericListener"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 80, "name": "is_character", "signature": "def is_character(self)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 84, "name": "is_terminator", "signature": "def is_terminator(self)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 88, "name": "is_recognized", "signature": "def is_recognized(self)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 542, "name": "__init__", "signature": "def __init__(self)"}, {"doc": "Classify a single utterance into an :class:`AlphanumericMatch`.", "kind": "method", "line": 570, "name": "classify", "signature": "def classify(self, raw_text)"}, {"doc": "Classify a potentially multi-token utterance.\n\nFirst tries to classify the utterance as a whole; if that returns\n``NONE`` and the utterance contains multiple tokens, falls back to\nclassifying each token individually (so ``\"h o m e\"`` resolves to\nfour ``CHARACTER`` events).  The returned list preserves order and\nstops after the first ``STOPPED`` match.", "kind": "method", "line": 606, "name": "classify_sequence", "signature": "def classify_sequence(self, raw_text)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 637, "name": "_resolve", "signature": "def _resolve(self, text)"}, {"doc": "Recognise speller patterns like ``\"A for Alpha\"`` / ``\"B as in Boy\"``.\n\nThe text is split on a small set of connector phrases (``\"for\"``,\n``\"as in\"``, ``\"is for\"``, ``\"like\"``).  We accept the utterance\nwhen:\n\n* The left side resolves through :attr:`_lookup` to a single\n  alphabetic character -- so ``\"a\"``, ``\"bee\"``, ``\"alpha\"``,\n  ``\"whiskey\"`` are all valid spellers, but ``\"one\"`` (digit) or\n  ``\"hash\"`` (special) are not.\n* The right side is a single word whose first character matches\n  the resolved letter (case-insensitive).  This covers both the\n  NATO codewords (``\"A for Alpha\"``) and free-form memory aids\n  (``\"B as in Boy\"``, ``\"M for Mary\"``) without us having to\n  enumerate every English word.\n\nWithout this pattern handler the matcher's word-by-word fallback\nwould tokenise ``\"A for Alpha\"`` into ``a`` + ``4`` + ``a``,\nbecause ``\"for\"`` is a registered homophone of ``\"four\"`` in the\ndigit vocabulary -- so we have to short-circuit the whole-utterance\nmatch here.\n\nConnectors are checked most-specific-first so ``\"a is for alpha\"``\nsplits on ``\"is for\"`` before the bare ``\"for\"`` substring inside\nit has a chance to match.  When a connector splits the text but\nthe halves don't validate (e.g. ``\"a for bravo\"``) we ``continue``\nto try the next connector instead of returning, so an unrelated\nsubstring collision can't poison a later valid match.", "kind": "method", "line": 652, "name": "_resolve_spelled_letter", "signature": "def _resolve_spelled_letter(self, text)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 705, "name": "_char_accepted", "signature": "def _char_accepted(self, char)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 808, "name": "__init__", "signature": "def __init__(self, callback)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 829, "name": "__call__", "signature": "def __call__(self, event)"}, {"doc": "The currently assembled text.", "kind": "method", "line": 840, "name": "text", "signature": "def text(self)"}, {"doc": "Whether a stop command has been received.", "kind": "method", "line": 845, "name": "stopped", "signature": "def stopped(self)"}, {"doc": "The underlying :class:`AlphanumericMatcher`.", "kind": "method", "line": 850, "name": "matcher", "signature": "def matcher(self)"}, {"doc": "Programmatically clear the buffer.", "kind": "method", "line": 854, "name": "clear", "signature": "def clear(self)"}, {"doc": "Remove and return the last character, or ``None`` if empty.", "kind": "method", "line": 865, "name": "undo", "signature": "def undo(self)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 879, "name": "_process_utterance", "signature": "def _process_utterance(self, line)"}, {"doc": "Speak the TTS phrase for ``char`` if a TTS backend is wired.", "kind": "method", "line": 941, "name": "_speak_character", "signature": "def _speak_character(self, char)"}, {"doc": "Ask the TTS backend to play its error beep, if it supports one.\n\nCalled from the unrecognised-utterance branch so the user hears\na short audible cue that their last word was ignored.  Tolerates\nbackends that don't implement ``play_error`` (e.g. plain\nduck-typed stubs that only have ``say``) by checking for the\nmethod first.", "kind": "method", "line": 957, "name": "_play_error_feedback", "signature": "def _play_error_feedback(self)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 1063, "name": "on_event", "signature": "def on_event(event)"}]}, {"doc": "Load pre-computed sentence embeddings from a packaged TSV file.  Embedding library-level string constants (the default yes/no phrases used by ``Confirm`` prompts, for example) is relatively slow – the first ``PhraseMatcher`` for them can take a couple of seconds to build at runtime while the embedding model forward-passes each phrase.  That cost is entirely deterministic: the phrases and the model don't change between runs, so there's no reason to pay for it repeatedly.  This module ships those embeddings as *data* instead of *computation*:  1. ``scripts/build-cached-embeddings.py`` embeds the library phrases once with a chosen embedding model/variant and writes the result to ``assets/cached_embeddings.tsv`` inside the package. 2. At import time, :class:`CachedEmbeddings` reads that TSV into a ``{phrase: vector}`` dict. 3. Anywhere the library needs an :class:`EmbeddingBackend`, it can wrap the real recognizer with a :class:`CachedEmbeddings` instance: cache hits return instantly, cache misses (typically incoming user utterances) fall through to the recognizer.  TSV format ---------- ``# key: value`` header lines followed by one phrase per data line::  # model_name: embeddinggemma-300m # model_variant: q4 # embedding_dim: 768 # phrase_count: 18 yes\\\\t0.0123\\\\t-0.0456\\\\t...", "id": "python/src/moonshine_voice/cached_embeddings.py", "kind": "module", "label": "cached_embeddings.py", "language": "py", "sha256": "969c1f78cba4a33f", "symbol_count": 19, "symbols": [{"doc": "Narrow form of :class:`moonshine_voice.EmbeddingBackend`.\n\nRedefined here so this module doesn't import ``dialog_flow`` (which\nwould create a cycle).", "kind": "class", "line": 45, "name": "_EmbeddingBackend", "signature": "class _EmbeddingBackend(Protocol)"}, {"doc": "Return the absolute path of the packaged cached embeddings TSV.", "kind": "method", "line": 62, "name": "default_cached_embeddings_path", "signature": "def default_cached_embeddings_path()"}, {"doc": "A lookup table of pre-computed sentence embeddings.\n\nInstances duck-type as an embedding backend: call\n:meth:`calculate_embedding` with a phrase and you get back a vector.\nHits are served from memory in O(1); misses fall through to the\noptional ``fallback`` backend (typically the real\n:class:`IntentRecognizer`), or raise :class:`KeyError` if none is\nconfigured.\n\nParameters\n----------\npath:\n    Optional path to the TSV file.  Defaults to the TSV packaged with\n    :mod:`moonshine_voice`.  If the file is missing the cache is\n    simply empty – behaviour is then governed entirely by\n    ``fallback``.\nfallback:\n    Optional embedding backend consulted on cache misses.  If\n    ``None``, :meth:`calculate_embedding` raises on misses.\nexpected_model_name / expected_model_variant:\n    Optional strings.  When the TSV metadata does not match these,\n    the cache is *disabled* (wiped in-memory and a warning is logged\n    to stderr) so you never accidentally mix embeddings from\n    different models.  Leave ``None`` to skip validation.", "kind": "class", "line": 68, "name": "CachedEmbeddings", "signature": "class CachedEmbeddings"}, {"doc": "Write a TSV compatible with :class:`CachedEmbeddings`.\n\nReturns the number of phrase rows written.  Raises ``ValueError`` if a\nphrase contains a tab or newline character.", "kind": "method", "line": 260, "name": "write_cached_embeddings_tsv", "signature": "def write_cached_embeddings_tsv(path, entries)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 52, "name": "calculate_embedding", "signature": "def calculate_embedding(self, sentence)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 54, "name": "distance", "signature": "def distance(self, embedding_a, embedding_b)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 95, "name": "__init__", "signature": "def __init__(self)"}, {"doc": "``True`` when the cache has at least one usable entry.", "kind": "method", "line": 150, "name": "active", "signature": "def active(self)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 155, "name": "path", "signature": "def path(self)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 159, "name": "metadata", "signature": "def metadata(self)"}, {"doc": "Return the list of cached phrases (normalized keys).", "kind": "method", "line": 163, "name": "phrases", "signature": "def phrases(self)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 167, "name": "__len__", "signature": "def __len__(self)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 170, "name": "__contains__", "signature": "def __contains__(self, sentence)"}, {"doc": "Return the cached embedding or ``None`` if not present.", "kind": "method", "line": 175, "name": "get", "signature": "def get(self, sentence)"}, {"doc": "Return the embedding for ``sentence``.\n\nConsults the in-memory cache first, then falls through to the\nconfigured ``fallback`` backend.  Raises ``KeyError`` if neither\nyields a result.", "kind": "method", "line": 179, "name": "calculate_embedding", "signature": "def calculate_embedding(self, sentence)"}, {"doc": "Return the cosine similarity between two embedding vectors.\n\nThe cache itself does not implement similarity scoring – it\ndelegates to the configured ``fallback`` backend (typically an\n:class:`~moonshine_voice.IntentRecognizer`) so the underlying\nnative ``moonshine_calculate_embedding_distance`` C function is\nused.  Raises :class:`RuntimeError` when no fallback is\nconfigured.", "kind": "method", "line": 195, "name": "distance", "signature": "def distance(self, embedding_a, embedding_b)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 218, "name": "_load", "signature": "def _load(self, path)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 238, "name": "_parse_meta", "signature": "def _parse_meta(self, s)"}, {"doc": "Normalize a phrase for lookup.\n\nWe store and look up phrases in a case-folded, whitespace-stripped\nform so the cache is forgiving about minor casing differences in\nthe caller's registration.", "kind": "method", "line": 245, "name": "_normalize", "signature": "def _normalize(s)"}]}, {"doc": "Console-script entry point for the ``moonshine-voice`` package.  Installed as the ``moonshine-voice`` and ``moonshine`` commands via the ``[project.scripts]`` table in ``pyproject.toml``. This is a thin dispatcher: each subcommand runs the corresponding module's existing ``__main__`` demo, so ``moonshine-voice mic --language en`` is equivalent to the long-standing ``python -m moonshine_voice.mic_transcriber --language en``. Argument parsing, help text, and behaviour therefore live entirely in the individual modules and stay identical between the two invocation styles.", "id": "python/src/moonshine_voice/cli.py", "kind": "module", "label": "cli.py", "language": "py", "sha256": "f3a72dcda7b42dd7", "symbol_count": 3, "symbols": [{"kind": "function", "line": 50, "name": "_package_version", "signature": "def _package_version()"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 68, "name": "_usage", "signature": "def _usage()"}, {"doc": "Dispatch to a subcommand. Returns a process exit code.", "kind": "function", "line": 91, "name": "main", "signature": "def main(argv)"}]}, {"doc": "Generator-based dialog flow runner for Moonshine Voice.  A *flow* is an ordinary Python generator function that yields prompts to the runner and resumes with the user's answer:  from moonshine_voice import dialog_flow as df  def setup_wifi(d): ssid = yield d.ask(\"What's the name of your wifi network?\")  if not (yield d.confirm(f\"I heard, {ssid}. Is that right?\")): yield d.say(\"No problem, let's start over.\") return  password = yield d.ask( \"Please spell the wifi password.\", mode=df.SPELLED, )  if (yield d.confirm(\"Would you like to hear it read back?\")): yield d.say(f\"I heard: {df.spell_out(password)}\")  if (yield d.confirm(\"Apply these changes?\")): apply_wifi_config(ssid, password) yield d.say(\"Done. Your wifi is set up.\") else: yield d.say(\"Okay, nothing changed.\")  The :class:`DialogFlow` runner is a :class:`TranscriptEventListener`, so it composes with :class:`MicTranscriber` the same way :class:`IntentRecognizer`", "id": "python/src/moonshine_voice/dialog_flow.py", "kind": "module", "label": "dialog_flow.py", "language": "py", "sha256": "fe4770121a0dd101", "symbol_count": 94, "symbols": [{"doc": "Base class for values a flow function may yield to the runner.", "kind": "class", "line": 97, "name": "Prompt", "signature": "class Prompt"}, {"doc": "Speak ``text`` and resume the generator once playback has finished.", "kind": "class", "line": 102, "name": "Say", "signature": "class Say(Prompt)"}, {"doc": "Speak ``prompt`` and resume with the user's next utterance as a string.", "kind": "class", "line": 110, "name": "Ask", "signature": "class Ask(Prompt)"}, {"doc": "Speak ``prompt`` and resume with a bool (yes / no).", "kind": "class", "line": 147, "name": "Confirm", "signature": "class Confirm(Prompt)"}, {"doc": "Speak ``prompt`` and resume with the key of the matched option.\n\n``options`` maps option keys to canonical phrases.  Matching is done\nagainst the union of the key and its phrases, using the intent\nrecognizer when available and falling back to substring matching.", "kind": "class", "line": 166, "name": "Choose", "signature": "class Choose(Prompt)"}, {"doc": "Base class for dialog-flow exceptions.", "kind": "class", "line": 187, "name": "DialogError", "signature": "class DialogError(Exception)"}, {"doc": "Raised into / from a flow to abandon it entirely.", "kind": "class", "line": 191, "name": "DialogCancelled", "signature": "class DialogCancelled(DialogError)"}, {"doc": "Raised into / from a flow to restart it from the beginning.", "kind": "class", "line": 195, "name": "DialogRestart", "signature": "class DialogRestart(DialogError)"}, {"doc": "No utterance was received within the prompt's retry budget.", "kind": "class", "line": 199, "name": "NoInputError", "signature": "class NoInputError(DialogError)"}, {"doc": "Received an utterance but could not interpret it for this prompt.", "kind": "class", "line": 203, "name": "NoMatchError", "signature": "class NoMatchError(DialogError)"}, {"doc": "Minimal interface the phrase matcher needs from an embedding source.\n\n:class:`moonshine_voice.IntentRecognizer` satisfies this protocol via\nits :meth:`calculate_embedding` and :meth:`distance` methods – the\nlatter is a thin wrapper around the native\n``moonshine_calculate_embedding_distance`` C API so scoring happens\nin C rather than Python.", "kind": "class", "line": 212, "name": "EmbeddingBackend", "signature": "class EmbeddingBackend(Protocol)"}, {"doc": "Match an utterance to one of several key→phrases groups via embeddings.\n\nThis is a tiny wrapper around an :class:`EmbeddingBackend` (typically\nan :class:`IntentRecognizer`).  At construction time, the backend is\nused to compute an embedding for every phrase in every group; at\nmatch time, the utterance is embedded once and compared against\nevery phrase using cosine similarity.  The key of the best-scoring\nphrase (above ``threshold``) is returned, or *None* if nothing\nclears the threshold.\n\nUse this to replace string / substring matching on user utterances\nwith fuzzy, semantics-aware matching.\n\nExample::\n\n    yes_no = PhraseMatcher(\n        intent_recognizer,\n        {\"yes\": [\"yes\", \"sure\", \"please\"],\n         \"no\":  [\"no\", \"nope\", \"cancel\"]},\n        threshold=0.6,\n    )\n    assert yes_no.match(\"please go ahead\") == \"yes\"\n    assert yes_no.match(\"don't do that\")    == \"no\"", "kind": "class", "line": 229, "name": "PhraseMatcher", "signature": "class PhraseMatcher"}, {"doc": "Context object handed to a flow as its first argument.\n\nEach method returns a :class:`Prompt` that the flow yields; the runner\ncarries out the prompt and sends the result (if any) back into the\ngenerator.  ``Dialog`` itself performs no I/O, which keeps flows easy\nto unit-test: pass a ``Dialog`` to the flow, iterate the generator, and\ndrive it with ``.send()``.", "kind": "class", "line": 335, "name": "Dialog", "signature": "class Dialog"}, {"doc": "In-progress spelled / digit input buffered across utterances.", "kind": "class", "line": 432, "name": "_AlphaSession", "signature": "class _AlphaSession"}, {"doc": "Per-session state for a running flow.", "kind": "class", "line": 440, "name": "_ActiveFlow", "signature": "class _ActiveFlow"}, {"doc": "Runner that drives generator-based conversational flows.\n\nRegister flow functions against trigger phrases; completed transcript\nlines are routed either to the configured intent recognizer (when no\nflow is active) or to the currently suspended generator (when one is).\n\nThe runner is synchronous: when a flow yields a :class:`Say`, the\nrunner speaks and blocks until the utterance has been played, then\nresumes the generator.  When a flow yields an input-expecting prompt\n(:class:`Ask` / :class:`Confirm` / :class:`Choose`), the runner speaks\nthe prompt and returns control to the caller; the next completed\ntranscript line resumes the generator.\n\nArgs:\n    tts: Optional :class:`TextToSpeech` used to speak prompts.  If\n        set, prompts are spoken via ``tts.say(text)`` and the runner\n        blocks on ``tts.wait()`` before advancing the flow.\n    intent_recognizer: Optional :class:`IntentRecognizer` used for\n        matching trigger phrases to registered flows and for routing\n        utterances when no flow is active.  When omitted, trigger\n        matching falls back to case-insensitive substring matching.\n    transcriber: Reserved for future per-prompt biasing hooks.\n    speak_fn: Optional callable ``(text) -> None`` that speaks the text\n        and blocks until playback finishes.  Overrides ``tts``.  Useful\n        for tests and alternative TTS backends.\n    mute_fn: Optional callable ``(should_mute: bool) -> None`` invoked\n        before and after each spoken prompt so callers can silence the\n        microphone while the assistant is talking.\n    spell_feedback: If ``True`` (default), every character recognised\n        during a ``SPELLED`` / ``DIGITS`` prompt is spoken back to\n        the user using :func:`spoken_form` (``\"haitch\"`` for\n        ``\"h\"``, ``\"capital ay\"`` for ``\"A\"``, ``\"hash\"`` for\n        ``\"#\"``, etc.), and \"delete\" / \"backspace\" / \"undo\" /\n        \"scratch that\" commands are echoed as\n        ``\"deleting <character>\"`` so the user hears confirmation\n        that the right letter came off the end of the buffer.\n        Matches the behaviour of ``AlphanumericListener(tts=…)``\n        but routes through this runner's own\n        ``speak_fn``/``tts`` so the same mic-mute and logging\n        apply.  Pass ``spell_feedback=False`` to silence the\n        character-by-character echo (e.g. when no TTS is wired\n        up and audible output would just be log spam).\n    spelling_mode_fn: Optional callable\n        ``(active: bool) -> None`` invoked whenever the runner\n        enters or leaves a ``SPELLED`` / ``DIGITS`` prompt.  Wire\n        this to the underlying transcriber's\n        ``set_transcribe_flags`` to flip\n        ``MOONSHINE_FLAG_SPELLING_MODE`` on only while spelled\n        input is expected, so the C++ spelling-CNN fusion path is\n        used for password / code / digit dictation but doesn't\n        perturb free-form recognition or trigger-phrase matching.\n        Pairs with constructing the transcriber with a\n        ``spelling_model_path``; when no model is loaded the flag\n        is a no-op so leaving this ``None`` is also fine.\n    log_io: If ``True``, every utterance the runner receives from\n        the STT and every prompt it asks the TTS to speak is\n        logged to stderr in a clean ``user: …`` / ``assistant: …``\n        format.  Distinct from ``debug``: ``log_io`` is the\n        user-facing dialogue transcript (just inputs and\n        outputs), while ``debug`` is the verbose internal\n        stage-transition trace with timings.  Off by default so\n        existing callers that already format their own\n        transcript via ``speak_fn`` or a transcript listener\n        don't end up with duplicate lines; turn it on for a\n        quick inline trace when you don't care to wire up your\n        own logging.\n    ignore_stt_during_tts: If ``True`` (default), every utterance\n        that arrives while the runner is mid-prompt (i.e. the\n        TTS is actively speaking) is dropped before it can\n        advance the flow, match a global trigger, or fall\n        through to the intent recognizer.  This is a software\n        guard on top of the optional hardware ``mute_fn`` —\n        ``mute_fn`` minimises self-capture but on devices with\n        weak echo cancellation the STT can still latch onto\n        in-flight audio captured just before the mute, or onto\n        speaker bleed that the cancellation didn't fully\n        suppress.  Disable (``False``) only when you have\n        reliable echo cancellation *and* want barge-in: callers\n        still get the utterance via the regular\n        ``TranscriptEventListener`` path.\n    success_beep_fn: Optional callable ``() -> None`` invoked the\n        moment a completed transcript line is recognized — i.e.\n        it matched a trigger phrase or was successfully\n        interpreted as the answer to an active prompt — and\n        *before* any TTS response begins.  Gives the user a\n        short audible cue that \"I heard you and understood\"\n        before the assistant starts replying.  When omitted,\n        falls back to ``tts.play_success()`` if the configured\n        ``tts`` exposes one (e.g. the bundled\n        :class:`TextToSpeech`); pass any callable to override\n        (e.g. play a custom WAV) or ``lambda: None`` to\n        silence.\n    error_beep_fn: Optional callable ``() -> None`` invoked when\n        a completed transcript line *isn't* recognized — no\n        trigger matched, no active flow could interpret it as\n        an answer, and no global handler took it.  Pairs with\n        ``success_beep_fn`` so misrecognitions don't end in\n        silence: the user hears a distinct \"didn't get that\"\n        cue immediately, and the runner then reprompts /\n        abandons / forwards to the intent recognizer as before.\n        Same fallback as ``success_beep_fn`` — auto-wired to\n        ``tts.play_error()`` when available.", "kind": "class", "line": 453, "name": "DialogFlow", "signature": "class DialogFlow(TranscriptEventListener)"}, {"kind": "class", "line": 1619, "name": "_Reprompt", "signature": "class _Reprompt(Exception)"}, {"kind": "class", multi-utterance spelled / digit\ndictation).", "kind": "class", "line": 1629, "name": "_PartialInput", "signature": "class _PartialInput(Exception)"}, {"doc": "Space-joined spoken-form phrase that also iterates token-by-token.\n\nA ``str`` so ``f\"I heard: {spell_out(password)}\"`` interpolates as\nthe natural joined phrase (``\"ess ee ay bee\"``), but with\n``__iter__`` overridden to yield ``[\"ess\", \"ee\", \"ay\", \"bee\"]``.\nThat keeps backwards-compat with the older list-returning\n:func:`spell_out` API: a caller that wrote\n``\" \".join(spell_out(password))`` still gets the joined phrase\nback instead of the character-by-character ``\"e s s   e e   a y\nb e e\"`` you'd get from plain ``str`` iteration.", "kind": "class", "line": 1635, "name": "_SpelledPhrase", "signature": "class _SpelledPhrase(str)"}, {"doc": "Return ``s`` as a TTS-friendly spoken-form phrase.\n\nEach character is rendered as a phrase the TTS engine can pronounce\nunambiguously (letters use spelling-alphabet sounds like ``\"haitch\"``\nfor ``\"h\"``, upper-case letters are prefixed with ``\"capital \"``,\ndigits become word form, common symbols use their spoken name) and\nthe per-character phrases are joined with a single space.  The\nreturn value is a ``str`` subclass (:class:`_SpelledPhrase`) so it\ndrops cleanly into both an ``f\"I heard: {spell_out(password)}\"``\ninterpolation *and* a ``\" \".join(spell_out(password))`` call —\nboth produce the same joined phrase.  The per-character mapping\nlives in :func:`spoken_form` in ``alphanumeric_listener.py`` so\nthe :class:`AlphanumericListener`'s TTS repeat-back and this\nfunction can't drift apart.\n\n``spell_out(\"Hi#1\")`` renders as ``\"capital haitch eye hash\none\"`` (and iterates as\n``[\"capital\", \"haitch\", \"eye\", \"hash\", \"one\"]``).  Empty strings\nproduce ``\"\"``.  This is for *speaking* strings back at the user,\nnot for matching their input (that's\n:class:`AlphanumericMatcher`'s job); callers that need the\nstrict per-character list (e.g. for custom pacing between\ntokens) can use ``[spoken_form(c) for c in s]`` directly.", "kind": "method", "line": 1656, "name": "spell_out", "signature": "def spell_out(s)"}, {"doc": "Truncate ``text`` for debug logs so we don't spam the terminal.", "kind": "method", "line": 1684, "name": "_summarise", "signature": "def _summarise(text, max_len)"}, {"doc": "Play the success / error beeps and a reference tone, then return.\n\nUsed by ``--play-test-beeps`` to isolate \"speech audible, beeps\nnot\" issues without going through mic + flow.  Plays in order:\n\n1. Success beep (ascending two-tone, ~0.41 s incl. pad).\n2. One second of silence.\n3. Error beep (descending two-tone, ~0.48 s incl. pad).\n4. One second of silence.\n5. A 500 ms 440 Hz reference tone at ~0.5 amplitude — twice as\n   loud as the beeps' 0.25 amplitude — so a \"reference audible\n   but beeps not\" outcome points at the beep waveform (raise\n   amplitude or extend the lead-silence pad) rather than at\n   the audio stack.\n\nRoutes through the same :class:`TextToSpeech` instance that the\nmain flow would use, so the diagnostic exercises the exact same\nstream-open / play / wait code path (and thus the same\nPortAudio / PipeWire / ALSA shim) that the real beeps go\nthrough.", "kind": "method", "line": 1704, "name": "_run_beep_diagnostic", current :class:`Dialog` (a fresh one when\nno flow is active) and may return a :class:`Prompt` to speak, or\n*None*.  It may also raise :class:`DialogCancelled` or\n:class:`DialogRestart` to influence the active flow.", "kind": "method", "line": 680, "name": "register_global", "signature": "def register_global(self, trigger_phrase, handler)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 691, "name": "_invalidate_trigger_matcher", "signature": "def _invalidate_trigger_matcher(self)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 697, "name": "is_active", "signature": "def is_active(self)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 702, "name": "active_trigger", "signature": "def active_trigger(self)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 707, "name": "registered_flows", "signature": "def registered_flows(self)"}, {"doc": "Tag any transcript line that opens while we're talking.\n\nStreaming ASRs commonly finalise a ``LineCompleted`` event\nseveral hundred milliseconds *after* the audio that produced\nit arrived, so a transcript started while the assistant was\nspeaking often only completes once ``_speak`` has already\nreturned.  Decide self-capture status at line-birth instead\nof completion: if a line was opened during TTS playback we\nrecord its ID here, then drop it on completion in\n:meth:`on_line_completed` regardless of how long the ASR took\nto finalise it.  Lines that open *after* TTS ends are accepted\nwith no added latency – the user can talk the moment the\nassistant stops, no grace window required.\n\nOnly takes effect when ``ignore_stt_during_tts`` is on; when\nit's off (true barge-in mode) we leave the set empty so every\nline completes through to :meth:`process_utterance`.", "kind": "method", "line": 712, "name": "on_line_started", "signature": "def on_line_started(self, event)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 746, "name": "on_line_completed", "signature": "def on_line_completed(self, event)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 772, "name": "on_error", "signature": "def on_error(self, event)"}, {"doc": "Route an utterance.\n\nReturns ``True`` if it was consumed by a flow or a global handler,\n``False`` otherwise. Returns ``True`` if there was one.", "kind": "method", "line": 1156, "name": "cancel_active", "signature": "def cancel_active(self)"}, {"doc": "Speak ``text`` through the configured TTS, outside any flow.\n\nPublic counterpart to flows yielding ``d.say(...)``: lets the\napplication deliver welcome messages, status announcements,\nerror notifications, and the like without first registering a\nsingle-shot flow.  Safe to call concurrently with an active\nflow – it just routes through the same ``_speak`` path the\nrunner uses for in-flow prompts, so:\n\n* ``mute_fn`` is invoked around playback (if configured) so\n  the mic is silenced while the assistant talks.\n* ``_speaking`` is set across playback and the\n  ``on_line_started`` hook tags any STT lines that open during\n  this window as self-capture, so they get dropped on\n  completion (when ``ignore_stt_during_tts`` is on).\n* ``log_io`` emits a clean ``assistant: ...`` line, matching\n  the format used for in-flow speech.\n\nBlocks until playback finishes – mirrors the behaviour of an\nin-flow ``Say``.  Empty / ``None`` ``text`` is a no-op.  When\nno ``speak_fn`` or ``tts`` is configured the text is printed\nto stdout (same fallback as in-flow ``Say``).", "kind": "method", "line": 1169, "name": "say", "signature": "def say(self, text)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 1199, "name": "_invoke_global", "signature": "def _invoke_global(self, trigger_phrase)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 1236, "name": "_interpret_answer", "signature": "def _interpret_answer(self, prompt, utterance, active)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 1247, "name": "_interpret_ask", "signature": "def _interpret_ask(self, prompt, utterance, active)"}, {"doc": "Drive the AlphanumericMatcher session for SPELLED / DIGITS.\n\nThe user is expected to dictate one character per utterance (e.g.\nspelling a password over a microphone), so each completed\nutterance only updates an in-progress buffer. This routes through\nthe configured ``success_beep_fn`` / ``error_beep_fn`` (or\ntheir ``tts.play_*`` auto-wiring) and provides three levels\nof visibility for \"no beep heard\" debugging:\n\n* No-op when the callback is not configured, but the\n  first such miss for each kind is reported once on\n  stderr so the auto-wiring failing silently doesn't\n  look like a configured-but-broken beep. (0.92)\n\nExample as TranscriptEventListener:\n    >>> recognizer = IntentRecognizer(\"path/to/embedding-model\")\n    >>> recognizer.register_intent(\"turn on the lights\", lambda c, u, s: print(f\"Lights on!\"))\n    >>> transcriber.add_listener(recognizer)  # Now intents are recognized automatically", "kind": "class", "line": 42, "name": "IntentRecognizer", "signature": "class IntentRecognizer(TranscriptEventListener)"}, {"doc": "Alias for ``canonical_phrase`` (backward compatibility).", "kind": "method", "line": 37, "name": "trigger_phrase", "signature": "def trigger_phrase(self)"}, {"doc": "Initialize an intent recognizer.\n\nArgs:\n    model_path: Path to the directory containing the embedding model files\n               (ONNX model and tokenizer.bin).\n    model_arch: The embedding model architecture to use.\n               Currently only GEMMA_300M is supported.\n    model_variant: Model variant to load: \"fp32\", \"fp16\", \"q8\", \"q4\",\n                  or \"q4f16\".
