returns the IPA string (single segment).", "kind": "method", "line": 546, "name": "moonshine_text_to_phonemes_string", "signature": "def moonshine_text_to_phonemes_string(grapheme_to_phonemizer_handle, text, options)"}, {"doc": "Internal class to load and wrap the Moonshine C library.", "kind": "class", "line": 583, "name": "_MoonshineLib", "signature": "class _MoonshineLib"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 244, "name": "__str__", "signature": "def __str__(self)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 272, "name": "__str__", "signature": "def __str__(self)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 302, "name": "__str__", "signature": "def __str__(self)"}, {"doc": "Return a string representation of the transcript.", "kind": "method", "line": 317, "name": "__str__", "signature": "def __str__(self)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 589, "name": "__new__", "signature": "def __new__(cls)"}, {"doc": "Load the Moonshine shared library.", "kind": "method", "line": 595, "name": "_load_library", "signature": "def _load_library(self)"}, {"doc": "Setup ctypes function signatures for the C API.", "kind": "method", "line": 642, "name": "_setup_function_signatures", "signature": "def _setup_function_signatures(self)"}, {"doc": "Get the loaded library.", "kind": "method", "line": 888, "name": "lib", "signature": "def lib(self)"}]}, {"doc": "Text-to-speech via the Moonshine C API.", "id": "python/src/moonshine_voice/tts.py", "kind": "module", "label": "tts.py", "language": "py", "sha256": "c307c5490ade380a", "symbol_count": 44, "symbols": [{"doc": "Queued utterance for the background synthesis worker.", "kind": "class", "line": 33, "name": "_SayRequest", "signature": "class _SayRequest"}, {"doc": "Synthesized audio ready for the playback worker.", "kind": "class", "line": 43, "name": "_PlayItem", "signature": "class _PlayItem"}, {"doc": "Queued beep marker; routed through the say queue so it plays in\nthe same order as any in-flight :meth:`TextToSpeech.say` calls\nrather than racing ahead on the play queue.\n\n``kind`` selects which packaged WAV to play:\n\n* ``\"error\"`` – ``assets/error.wav``, played to signal a\n  misrecognition or a rejected utterance.\n* ``\"success\"`` – ``assets/success.wav``, played to signal a\n  recognized utterance, just before the TTS response.", "kind": "class", "line": 51, "name": "_BeepRequest", "signature": "class _BeepRequest"}, {"doc": "Return ``(samples_float32, sample_rate)`` for the named beep.\n\nLoaded lazily from the packaged ``assets/<kind>.wav`` file the first\ntime it's requested and cached for the lifetime of the process.\nRaises :class:`ValueError` for unknown kinds and lets file errors\nfrom :func:`load_wav_file` propagate (so a missing asset is loud,\nnot silent — the symptom otherwise would be the same \"no beep\"\nissue we just spent two iterations debugging).", "kind": "method", "line": 88, "name": "_load_beep_samples", "signature": "def _load_beep_samples(np, kind)"}, {"doc": "Import numpy and sounddevice for `TextToSpeech.say`; raise MoonshineError if missing.", "kind": "method", "line": 116, "name": "_import_say_audio_deps", "signature": "def _import_say_audio_deps()"}, {"doc": "Return PortAudio's current default output device index, if any.\n\nWraps ``sd.default.device`` because sounddevice exposes that as a\ncustom ``_InputOutputPair`` NamedTuple, *not* a plain ``tuple`` /\n``list``, so an ``isinstance(..., (tuple, list))`` check on it\nmisses and the diagnostic flag would silently never light up.\nFalls back through several access patterns so a minor sounddevice\nAPI change can't suppress the \"current default\" annotation.", "kind": "method", "line": 129, "name": "_resolve_default_output_index", "signature": "def _resolve_default_output_index(sd)"}, {"doc": "Return human-readable output device descriptions for diagnostics.\n\nEach entry is formatted ``\"[idx] name (hostapi: NAME)\"`` so a\ncaller can paste either the index or a substring of the name into\n:class:`TextToSpeech`'s ``output_device`` argument (or the\n``--output-device`` flag of the CLI demo).  The first line of the\nreturned list flags PortAudio's default output device — on\nRaspberry Pi this is often *not* the one with speakers attached\n(e.g. HDMI when the user has wired up the 3.5 mm jack), and a\nsilent assistant with no errors in the logs is exactly the\nsymptom of the wrong device being selected.\n\nUse :class:`TextToSpeech`'s ``output_device`` to pin to a\nspecific one when ``None`` (= host default) doesn't reach a\nspeaker.", "kind": "method", "line": 163, "name": "list_output_devices", "signature": "def list_output_devices()"}, {"doc": "PortAudio device indices with at least one output channel, and host API name.", "kind": "method", "line": 219, "name": "_say_enumerate_output_devices", "signature": "def _say_enumerate_output_devices(sd)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 241, "name": "_say_device_lines", "signature": "def _say_device_lines(outs)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 245, "name": "_say_device_spec_key", "signature": "def _say_device_spec_key(device)"}, {"doc": "Pick the best output sample rate the device will actually open.\n\nReturns ``(target_sr, last_error)``. ``target_sr`` is ``None`` if no\ncandidate rate works (in which case ``last_error`` is the PortAudio\nerror from the source-rate probe and useful for diagnostics).\nOtherwise ``target_sr`` is:\n\n1. ``source_sr`` if the device accepts it natively (no resampling),\n2. 48000 Hz when supported (cleanest fallback for 24 kHz input),\n3. otherwise the largest supported rate that is an integer multiple\n   or divisor of ``source_sr``,\n4. otherwise the supported rate closest to ``source_sr``.\n\nProbes that fail with ``paDeviceUnavailable`` (-9985) are retried\na few times with a short backoff: that error code is transient on\nexclusive-access ALSA devices (e.g. USB DACs) when a previous\n``sd.play()`` stream hasn't fully released the device yet, and a\nsingle failed probe shouldn't be enough to disqualify a rate the\ndevice actually supports.", "kind": "method", "line": 270, "name": "_select_output_sample_rate", "signature": "def _select_output_sample_rate(sd)"}, {"doc": "Numpy-only linear-interpolation resample of mono float32 audio.\n\nLinear interpolation is the highest-quality resampler we can build\nwithout scipy; for clean integer ratios (e.g. 24 kHz -> 48 kHz) the\nnew sample positions land exactly between source samples, so the\ninterpolation error stays small.", "kind": "method", "line": 339, "name": "_resample_linear", "signature": "def _resample_linear(np, samples, source_sr, target_sr)"}, {"doc": "Return ``(pcm, sample_rate)`` from a ``clone`` spec.\n\nAccepts either a path to a WAV file on disk (``str`` / ``Path``), which is\ndecoded with :func:`moonshine_voice.utils.load_wav_file` (16/24-bit PCM,\nstereo mixed down to mono), or a ``(pcm, sample_rate)`` pair where ``pcm``\nis mono float PCM in ``[-1, 1]`` (any sequence or numpy array) and\n``sample_rate`` is in Hz.", "kind": "method", "line": 360, "name": "_normalize_clone_argument", "signature": "def _normalize_clone_argument(clone)"}, {"doc": "Transcribe a clone reference clip so ZipVoice gets text aligned with the audio.", "kind": "method", "line": 389, "name": "_autotranscribe_clone_pcm", "signature": "def _autotranscribe_clone_pcm(pcm, sample_rate)"}, {"doc": "Return PortAudio output device index, or None for the host default stream device.", "kind": "method", "line": 423, "name": "_say_resolve_output_index", "signature": "def _say_resolve_output_index(spec_key, outs)"}, {"doc": "On-device TTS using Moonshine (Kokoro / Piper and language assets under ``g2p_root``).\n\nRequired assets are resolved with ``moonshine_get_tts_dependencies`` and, unless you pass\n``download=False`` and ``asset_root``, downloaded from ``https://download.moonshine.ai/tts/``.\n\nThe ``language`` tag is validated against the native TTS catalog before download\n(`MoonshineTtsLanguageError` lists supported tags).     If ``voice`` is set, it is checked against\nvoices reported as ``found`` for that language under the resolved asset root\n(`MoonshineTtsVoiceError` lists downloaded ids then catalog ids available for download).\nWith ``download=True``, a voice that is catalogued but not yet on disk is downloaded automatically.\nUse a ``kokoro_``, ``piper_``, or ``zipvoice_`` prefix on ``voice`` to pin the vocoder (e.g.\n``kokoro_af_heart``, ``zipvoice_american_female``). ZipVoice is a zero-shot voice cloner: besides\nthe built-in ``zipvoice_<id>`` reference voices you can clone your own by passing ``clone`` —\neither a path to a ``.wav`` file or a ``(pcm, sample_rate)`` pair of mono float PCM — along with\n(recommended) ``clone_transcript``, the text spoken in the reference clip (when omitted, the clip\nis auto-transcribed with Moonshine ASR before cloning). When ``clone`` is set\nthe ZipVoice engine is used automatically; passing ``voice`` together with ``clone``\nraises `MoonshineError`.\nUse `list_tts_languages` and\n`list_tts_voices` (``present`` / ``downloadable``) or `get_tts_voice_catalog` to discover options.", "kind": "class", "line": 453, "name": "TextToSpeech", "signature": "class TextToSpeech"}, {"doc": "Parse ``KEY=value`` pairs from repeated ``--options`` (values stay strings except booleans).", "kind": "method", "line": 1333, "name": "_parse_options_cli", "signature": "def _parse_options_cli(pairs)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 1356, "name": "_write_wav_mono_pcm16", "signature": "def _write_wav_mono_pcm16(path, samples, sample_rate_hz)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 295, "name": "_try", "signature": "def _try(sr)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 477, "name": "__init__", "signature": "def __init__(self, language)"}, {"doc": "Shared playback/queue state used by both the from-files and ZipVoice-from-memory paths.", "kind": "method", "line": 604, "name": "_init_playback_state", "signature": "def _init_playback_state(self, output_device, volume, debug)"}, {"doc": "Create a ZipVoice synthesizer from an in-memory reference clip (mono float PCM).", "kind": "method", "line": 636, "name": "_init_zipvoice_from_clone", "signature": "def _init_zipvoice_from_clone(self, language)"}, {"doc": "Print a one-liner identifying the PortAudio device we opened.\n\nEmitted only when ``debug=True`` (silent during normal use). When enabled\nit helps diagnose a silent runtime with no errors in the trace, which is\nalmost always the *wrong* PortAudio device being selected (e.g. HDMI on a\nPi when speakers are on the 3.5 mm jack); the log shows *which* device the\nworker actually opened.\n\nIncludes the host-API name and the default sample rate the\ndevice claims to support; on top of that, when the resolved\ndevice is the host default we list the other available\noutputs so the user can pin a specific one via\n``TextToSpeech(output_device=...)`` (or the CLI's\n``--output-device`` flag).\n\nOnly emitted when ``debug=True``; it is silent during normal use.", "kind": "method", "line": 734, "name": "_announce_resolved_device", "signature": "def _announce_resolved_device(self, sd, resolved)"}, {"doc": "Emit a timestamped trace line to stderr when ``debug=True``.\n\nSame shape as ``DialogFlow._log`` so traces from the two\ncomponents can be read together: each line shows the wall\ntime since the previous log line and since the first log\nline of this instance.  Off by default — TTS traces are\nverbose and only useful for diagnosing playback problems\n(e.g. why a beep didn't seem to play).", "kind": "method", "line": 793, "name": "_log", "signature": "def _log(self, msg)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 819, "name": "_c_options_for_create", "signature": "def _c_options_for_create(self)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 828, "name": "language", "signature": "def language(self)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 832, "name": "asset_root", "signature": "def asset_root(self)"}, {"doc": "Synthesize ``text`` to PCM float samples ``(-1..1)`` and sample rate in Hz.", "kind": "method", "line": 835, "name": "synthesize", "signature": "def synthesize(self, text)"}, {"doc": "Synthesize speech directly from IPA ``phonemes``, skipping grapheme-to-phoneme conversion.\n\n``phonemes`` is an International Phonetic Alphabet string in the same format produced by\n:meth:`~moonshine_voice.g2p.GraphemeToPhonemizer.to_ipa`. Passing the raw\nphonemes for the same language yields audio equivalent to :meth:`synthesize` on the original\ntext, but lets you inspect or edit the phonemes in between (e.g. to fix a name's\npronunciation). Returns PCM float samples ``(-1..1)`` and the sample rate in Hz.", "kind": "method", "line": 856, "name": "synthesize_from_phonemes", "signature": "def synthesize_from_phonemes(self, phonemes)"}, {"doc": "Queue ``text`` for synthesis and playback, returning immediately.\n\n``text`` may be a single string or a list of strings. A list is equivalent to calling\n``say`` once per element in order.\n\nUtterances are played in order. Synthesis of the next utterance is pipelined with playback\nof the current one so there is minimal gap between consecutive utterances. Call `stop` to\ncancel all pending utterances and halt the currently-playing audio.\n\nUses `synthesize` for audio generation; ``options`` is passed through unchanged.\n\n``device`` may be ``None`` (host default output), a PortAudio device index, a decimal string\nindex, or a substring of the device name (case-insensitive). If there are no output devices,\nthe index is invalid, or no name matches, the error is raised on the calling thread before\nthe utterance is enqueued.", "kind": "method", "line": 883, "name": "say", "signature": "def say(self, text)"}, {"doc": "Play the bundled \"error\" beep and return immediately.\n\nPlays ``assets/error.wav`` queued through the same pipeline as\n:meth:`say` — so if a previous ``say`` hasn't finished speaking\nyet the beep plays right after it, rather than racing ahead.\nUse :meth:`wait` / :meth:`is_talking` to track playback.\n\nPairs with :meth:`play_success`: callers that want audible\nfeedback for whether speech recognition succeeded can call\n:meth:`play_success` on a recognized utterance and\n:meth:`play_error` on an unrecognized one.\n\n``device`` accepts the same values as :meth:`say` (``None`` =\nconstructor's ``output_device`` if set, otherwise host\ndefault; a PortAudio index, a decimal string index, or a\ncase-insensitive device-name substring).  Honouring the\nconstructor's ``output_device`` here matches :meth:`say`'s\nbehaviour — without that, callers who pin a specific output\ndevice for speech would get their cue beeps routed to the\nhost default and end up with audible speech but inaudible\nbeeps.", "kind": "method", "line": 928, "name": "play_error", "signature": "def play_error(self)"}, {"doc": "Play the bundled \"success\" beep and return immediately.\n\nCounterpart to :meth:`play_error` for positive feedback: plays\n``assets/success.wav`` confirming that the most recent\nutterance was recognized / accepted.  Same queueing rules as\n:meth:`play_error` — decoded once, cached, and ordered\nthrough the say queue so it never races ahead of an in-flight\n:meth:`say`.\n\n``device`` accepts the same values as :meth:`say` and falls\nback to the constructor's ``output_device`` when ``None``,\nfor the same reason as :meth:`play_error`.", "kind": "method", "line": 962, "name": "play_success", "signature": "def play_success(self)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 987, "name": "_ensure_say_workers", "signature": "def _ensure_say_workers(self)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 1005, "name": "_synth_worker", "signature": "def _synth_worker(self)"}, {"doc": "Synthesize a single utterance into a _PlayItem (runs on synthesis thread).", "kind": "method", "line": 1060, "name": "_synthesize_one", "signature": "def _synthesize_one(self, req, np)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 1069, "name": "_play_worker", "signature": "def _play_worker(self)"}, {"doc": "Resolve the device and play a single synthesized utterance (runs on playback thread).", "kind": "method", "line": 1097, "name": "_play_one", "signature": "def _play_one(self, item, sd, np)"}, {"doc": "Return ``True`` if utterances are queued, being synthesized, or currently playing.", "kind": "method", "line": 1242, "name": "is_talking", "signature": "def is_talking(self)"}, {"doc": "Block until all queued utterances have been synthesized and played.", "kind": "method", "line": 1255, "name": "wait", "signature": "def wait(self)"}, {"doc": "Clear the utterance queue and stop any audio currently playing.\n\nReturns once all pending utterances are discarded and the active playback (if any) has\nbeen halted. It is safe to call `say` again afterwards.", "kind": "method", "line": 1260, "name": "stop", "signature": "def stop(self)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 1288, "name": "close", "signature": "def close(self)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 1320, "name": "__enter__", "signature": "def __enter__(self)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 1323, "name": "__exit__", "signature": "def __exit__(self, exc_type, exc, tb)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 1326, "name": "__del__", "signature": "def __del__(self)"}]}, {"doc": "Utility functions for Moonshine Voice.", "id": "python/src/moonshine_voice/utils.py", "kind": "module", "label": "utils.py", "language": "py", "sha256": "32b527b32392b85e", "symbol_count": 3, "symbols": [{"doc": "Get the path to the assets directory included in the package.\n\nReturns:\n    Path object pointing to the assets directory\n\nExample:\n    >>> from moonshine_voice.utils import get_assets_path\n    >>> assets_path = get_assets_path()\n    >>> model_path = assets_path / \"tiny-en\"", "kind": "function", "line": 9, "name": "get_assets_path", "signature": "def get_assets_path()"}, {"doc": "Get the path to a specific model directory in the assets folder.\n\nArgs:\n    model_name: Name of the model directory (default: \"tiny-en\")\n\nReturns:\n    Path object pointing to the model directory\n\nExample:\n    >>> from moonshine_voice.utils import get_model_path\n    >>> model_path = get_model_path(\"tiny-en\")\n    >>> transcriber = Transcriber(str(model_path))", "kind": "function", "line": 27, "name": "get_model_path", "signature": "def get_model_path(model_name)"}, {"doc": "Load a WAV file and return audio data as float array and sample rate.\n\nSupports 16-bit and 24-bit PCM WAV files. Audio samples are normalized\nto the range [-1.0, 1.0].\n\nArgs:\n    file_path: Path to the WAV file\n\nReturns:\n    Tuple of (audio_data, sample_rate) where:\n    - audio_data: List of float samples in range [-1.0, 1.0]\n    - sample_rate: Sample rate in Hz\n\nRaises:\n    ValueError: If the file is not a valid WAV file\n    IOError: If the file cannot be read\n\nExample:\n    >>> from moonshine_voice.utils import load_wav_file\n    >>> audio_data, sample_rate = load_wav_file(\"audio.wav\")\n    >>> print(f\"Loaded {len(audio_data)} samples at {sample_rate} Hz\")", "kind": "function", "line": 47, "name": "load_wav_file", "signature": "def load_wav_file(file_path)"}]}, {"doc": "Tests the ``moonshine-voice`` console-script entry point.  The pip package installs a ``moonshine-voice`` command (and a ``moonshine`` alias) via ``[project.scripts]`` in ``pyproject.toml``. These tests exercise the installed script directly so that a broken entry point, a renamed subcommand, or a stale help table is caught before a release is published. They only touch the dispatcher (help / version / argument parsing) and never load models, so they run in well under a second.", "id": "python/tests/test_cli.py", "kind": "module", "label": "test_cli.py", "language": "py", "sha256": "3d58cbfe2b256855", "symbol_count": 8, "symbols": [{"doc": "Locate the installed console script, falling back to ``python -m``.\n\nConsole scripts are installed next to the interpreter running the tests, so\nwe look there first (this is the wheel-under-test in CI). If it is missing\nwe fall back to running the module, which still exercises the dispatcher.", "kind": "function", "line": 24, "name": "console_script", "signature": "def console_script(name)"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 40, "name": "run", "signature": "def run()"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 49, "name": "describe", "signature": "def describe(result)"}, {"doc": "Both the primary command and the short alias must be on PATH.", "kind": "function", "line": 58, "name": "test_console_scripts_are_installed", "signature": "def test_console_scripts_are_installed(name)"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 65, "name": "test_help_lists_every_command", "signature": "def test_help_lists_every_command()"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 72, "name": "test_version_reports_package_name", "signature": "def test_version_reports_package_name()"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 78, "name": "test_unknown_command_is_a_usage_error", "signature": "def test_unknown_command_is_a_usage_error()"}, {"doc": "``<command> --help`` must succeed and show the friendly command prefix.\n\nThis routes through the module's own argparse, so it also proves the\ndispatcher hands arguments off correctly and that the module's flags parse.", "kind": "function", "line": 84, "name": "test_subcommand_help_parses", "signature": "def test_subcommand_help_parses(command)"}]}, {"doc": "Tests that the code blocks in the documentation actually work.  Extracts fenced code blocks from the markdown files listed in DOC_FILES and checks each one, so that stale commands (for example a CLI flag that has been renamed) are caught before a release is published.  How a block is treated is controlled by an HTML comment placed on the line immediately before the opening fence (invisible in rendered markdown):  <!-- doc-test: skip -->         Not tested at all. <!-- doc-test: parse-only -->   The command is started with a short timeout. The test fails only if it exits with code 2 (an argparse usage error), so stale flags are caught even for commands that need a microphone or run forever. <!-- doc-test: expect-error --> The command must exit with a nonzero code. <!-- doc-test: run -->          Full execution (opt-in for python blocks).  Unannotated ``bash`` blocks are executed in full and must succeed. Unannotated ``python`` blocks are only checked for valid syntax, since many are illustrative fragments that reference variables defined in prose.", "id": "python/tests/test_docs.py", "kind": "module", "label": "test_docs.py", "language": "py", "sha256": "ab132aa01ac7c00b", "symbol_count": 10, "symbols": [{"kind": "class", "line": 60, "name": "DocBlock", "signature": "class DocBlock"}, {"doc": "Returns the doc-test mode from an annotation comment, or None.", "kind": "method", "line": 73, "name": "parse_annotation", "signature": "def parse_annotation(line)"}, {"doc": "Yields a DocBlock for every fenced code block in a markdown file.", "kind": "method", "line": 84, "name": "extract_blocks", "signature": "def extract_blocks(path)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 120, "name": "resolve_mode", "signature": "def resolve_mode(language, annotation)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 130, "name": "collect_all_blocks", "signature": "def collect_all_blocks()"}, {"doc": "Runs a bash block as a script, returning the CompletedProcess.\n\nRaises subprocess.TimeoutExpired if the timeout is hit; callers decide\nwhether that counts as a failure.", "kind": "method", "line": 137, "name": "run_bash_block", "signature": "def run_bash_block(block, cwd, timeout)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 158, "name": "check_python_syntax", "signature": "def check_python_syntax(block)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 171, "name": "describe", "signature": "def describe(result)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 185, "name": "test_doc_block", "signature": "def test_doc_block(block, tmp_path)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 68, "name": "test_id", "signature": "def test_id(self)"}]}, {"doc": "Regression test for issue #196.  ``MicTranscriber`` feeds microphone audio to the stream from PortAudio's capture callback, which runs on a high-priority, time-critical audio thread. The stream performs the actual (slow) transcription every ``update_interval``. If that transcription runs *inline* on the capture callback, the callback blocks for the full inference time and PortAudio reports ``input overflow`` -- exactly what was observed on a Raspberry Pi in https://github.com/moonshine-ai/moonshine/issues/196.  This test reproduces that behaviour without a real microphone, model, or the native library:  * ``FakeInputStream`` stands in for ``sounddevice.InputStream`` and drives the capture callback at the real-time block cadence, timing how long each callback takes to return. * ``FakeStream`` stands in for the real ``Stream``: ``add_audio`` buffers cheaply but, every ``update_interval`` worth of audio, blocks for ``SLOW_UPDATE_S`` to emulate a slow on-device inference.  A callback that returns slower than the block's wall-clock duration would overflow a real capture buffer, so we assert no callback ever exceeds that budget. With the transcription running inline (the buggy implementation) the update-triggering callbacks block ~``SLOW_UPDATE_S`` and the test fails; once ``MicTranscriber`` drains audio to a worker thread it passes.", "id": "python/tests/test_mic_transcriber_threading.py", "kind": "module", "label": "test_mic_transcriber_threading.py", "language": "py", "sha256": "df72f306e0116801", "symbol_count": 22, "symbols": [{"doc": "Minimal stand-in for ``moonshine_voice.transcriber.Stream``.\n\nMirrors the real stream's contract: ``add_audio`` is cheap except that\nevery ``update_interval`` of accumulated audio it runs a \"transcription\"\nthat blocks for ``SLOW_UPDATE_S``.", "kind": "class", "line": 47, "name": "FakeStream", "signature": "class FakeStream"}, {"doc": "Stand-in for ``Transcriber`` that hands back a ``FakeStream``.", "kind": "class", "line": 102, "name": "FakeTranscriber", "signature": "class FakeTranscriber"}, {"doc": "Stand-in for ``sounddevice.InputStream``.\n\nDelivers ``NUM_BLOCKS`` blocks of audio to the capture callback at the\nreal-time block cadence and records how long each callback takes. See core/STYLE_GUIDE.md for the rationale. Runs anywhere (macOS/Linux), needs only bash + grep + find, and is registered as the `check-banned-constructs` ctest.  Two tiers of enforcement:  1. Hard ban (zero tolerance, everywhere in first-party code): unsafe C string functions that have safe, bounded replacements.  2. Baseline gate (regression only): owning new/delete, C allocation calls, reinterpret_cast, and non-standard compiler builtins (__builtin_*, a GCC/Clang extension MSVC rejects) are tolerated where they already exist (recorded in core/.banned-constructs-allowlist) but blocked in any file not on that list. As modules are cleaned up, regenerate the baseline with `scripts/check-banned-constructs.sh --update-baseline` to lock in the improvement.  Usage: scripts/check-banned-constructs.sh                 # check (default) scripts/check-banned-constructs.sh --update-baseline", "id": "scripts/check-banned-constructs.sh", "kind": "module", "label": "check-banned-constructs.sh", "language": "sh", "sha256": "e784602c5c5c93cc", "symbol_count": 1, "symbols": [{"doc": "Print repo-relative paths of first-party files matching a regex, sorted.", "kind": "function", "line": 76, "name": "scan"}]}, {"doc": "Gate clang-tidy findings against a committed baseline so that only *newly introduced* problems fail the reliability run. This mirrors the approach in check-banned-constructs.sh: the current first-party code has a known, curated set of findings (see core/.clang-tidy-baseline) that are either benign for our \"C++ as a better C\" style or deliberately deferred; we accept those but refuse to let new ones creep in.  The baseline key is \"<check-name>\\t<repo-relative-path>\" (not line numbers, so it is stable across edits and reformatting). A finding is \"new\" if that pair is absent from the baseline. Adding a genuinely new class of bug -- e.g. the first clang-analyzer null-dereference in a file that never had one -- therefore fails the run, while shuffling lines around in an already-flagged file does not.  Usage: check-clang-tidy.sh --log FILE --baseline FILE --repo-root DIR [--update]  --update   Regenerate the baseline from FILE instead of comparing. Use this after intentionally changing the code/config, then commit the updated baseline.  Exit status: 0 = no new findings (or --update succeeded); 1 = new findings; 2 = usage / environment error.", "id": "scripts/check-clang-tidy.sh", "kind": "module", "label": "check-clang-tidy.sh", "language": "sh", "sha256": "3236d01fd4e87822", "symbol_count": 1, "symbols": [{"doc": "Extract a sorted, de-duplicated list of \"<check>\\t<relpath>\" pairs from a clang-tidy log. run-clang-tidy prints one \"path:line:col: warning: msg [check]\" line per finding (a finding in a shared header is repeated once per translation unit, which the de-dup collapses); a single line may list several comma-joined checks, each of which becomes its own pair.", "kind": "function", "line": 60, "name": "extract_keys"}]}, {"doc": "Compare Moonshine vs Piper Korean phonemes directly (no TTS/Whisper needed). Supports: - SentencePiece .model files (protobuf format) - HuggingFace tokenizer.json files  The BinTokenizer format is a simple binary format where each token is stored as: - 1 byte: length (if < 128) - 2 bytes: length (if >= 128, first byte has high bit set) - N bytes: token string  Empty tokens (length 0) are stored as a single 0x00 byte.  Usage: python convert_tokenizer.py <input_file> <output_file> python convert_tokenizer.py tokenizer.model tokenizer.bin python convert_tokenizer.py tokenizer.json tokenizer.bin", "id": "scripts/convert_tokenizer.py", "kind": "module", "label": "convert_tokenizer.py", "language": "py", "sha256": "813d409ba904c319", "symbol_count": 4, "symbols": [{"doc": "Write tokens to BinTokenizer format.", "kind": "function", "line": 29, "name": "write_bin_tokenizer", "signature": "def write_bin_tokenizer(tokens, output_path)"}, {"doc": "Convert SentencePiece .model file to BinTokenizer format.", "kind": "function", "line": 51, "name": "convert_sentencepiece", "signature": "def convert_sentencepiece(input_path, output_path)"}, {"doc": "Convert HuggingFace tokenizer.json to BinTokenizer format.", "kind": "function", "line": 84, "name": "convert_huggingface_json", "signature": "def convert_huggingface_json(input_path, output_path)"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 127, "name": "main", "signature": "def main()"}]}, {"doc": "Evaluate AlphanumericListener on the test-assets/alphanumeric dataset.  Each subfolder of ``test-assets/alphanumeric`` is named after the spoken word in its WAV files (``a``, ``b``, ..., ``z``, ``zero``, ``one``, ..., ``nine``). For every clip we run :class:`Transcriber.transcribe_without_streaming` (with ``MOONSHINE_FLAG_SPELLING_MODE`` so the C++ transcriber's spelling-CNN fusion runs end-to-end), synthesize a ``LineCompleted`` event from the resulting line(s), and feed that to a fresh :class:`AlphanumericListener`. The first ``CHARACTER`` event emitted by the listener is taken as the prediction.  Usage::  python scripts/eval-alphanumeric.py python scripts/eval-alphanumeric.py --dataset-dir test-assets/alphanumeric python scripts/eval-alphanumeric.py --no-spelling-model python scripts/eval-alphanumeric.py --verbose", "id": "scripts/eval-alphanumeric.py", "kind": "module", "label": "eval-alphanumeric.py", "language": "py", "sha256": "8e85c77c68bb4765", "symbol_count": 5, "symbols": [{"doc": "Resolve a folder name (e.g. ``\"a\"``, ``\"eight\"``) to its character.", "kind": "function", "line": 46, "name": "folder_name_to_expected_char", "signature": "def folder_name_to_expected_char(name, matcher)"}, {"doc": "Run transcription and return predictions for a single clip.\n\nReturns ``(predicted_char, raw_transcript_text)``:\n\n* ``predicted_char`` is the first ``CHARACTER`` event emitted by a\n  fresh :class:`AlphanumericListener` fed with synthesized\n  ``LineCompleted`` events, or ``None`` if nothing was recognised.\n  When ``transcribe_flags`` includes\n  ``MOONSHINE_FLAG_SPELLING_MODE`` the character is the C++ fusion\n  result; otherwise it's the matcher's lexical hit.\n* ``raw_transcript_text`` is ``\" | \"``-joined raw STT line text\n  (already the resolved character when fusion is enabled).", "kind": "function", "line": 54, "name": "predict_character", "signature": "def predict_character(transcriber, audio, sample_rate, transcribe_flags)"}, {"doc": "Pretty-print a confusion matrix with ``labels`` along both axes.", "kind": "function", "line": 106, "name": "print_confusion_matrix", "signature": "def print_confusion_matrix(matrix, labels, title)"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 138, "name": "main", "signature": "def main()"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 79, "name": "on_event", "signature": "def on_event(event)"}]}, {"doc": "Evaluate Moonshine English WER on LibriSpeech test-clean.  This script reproduces the LibriSpeech (clean) numbers reported in the Moonshine v2 paper (arXiv:2602.12241, Table 3) and lets us compare three different code paths so we can see where any accuracy gap comes from:  * ``moonshine_c``   - the shipped C++/ONNX library via the ``moonshine_voice`` Python bindings. These are the *quantized* ``.ort`` models that real users run. Uses ``transcribe_without_streaming`` (batch, whole-utterance). * ``moonshine_c_streaming`` - same library, but fed in small chunks through a streaming ``Stream`` (mimics issue #148's setup, which reports ~11.8% WER). * ``hf``            - the Hugging Face Transformers reference implementation with the *float* safetensors checkpoints. This is the code path the paper used to measure WER (see paper section 4.1.2), so it should reproduce ~4.49% for tiny.  WER is aggregated corpus-wide (total edits / total reference words), which is the Open ASR Leaderboard convention the paper follows. We also print the character-weighted per-utterance average that ``scripts/eval-model-accuracy.py`` uses, because that alternative aggregation is itself a source of confusion.  The VAD is disabled by default for the ``moonshine_c`` backend (the samples are known to be single speech utterances, so VAD segmentation only adds errors): ``vad_threshold=0`` and a very large ``vad_max_segment_duration`` so the whole clip is transcribed as one segment.  Examples", "id": "scripts/eval-librispeech.py", "kind": "module", "label": "eval-librispeech.py", "language": "py", "sha256": "0e1db71a772de112", "symbol_count": 10, "symbols": [{"kind": "function", "line": 87, "name": "parse_args", "signature": "def parse_args()"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 149, "name": "detect_text_column", "signature": "def detect_text_column(sample)"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 158, "name": "load_eval_dataset", "signature": "def load_eval_dataset(args)"}, {"doc": "Return (float32 mono @16kHz, sample_rate) from a non-decoded audio field.", "kind": "function", "line": 172, "name": "decode_audio", "signature": "def decode_audio(audio_field)"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 192, "name": "make_moonshine_c_backend", "signature": "def make_moonshine_c_backend(args, streaming)"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 233, "name": "make_hf_backend", "signature": "def make_hf_backend(args)"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 282, "name": "main", "signature": "def main()"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 211, "name": "transcribe_batch", "signature": "def transcribe_batch(audio, sample_rate)"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 217, "name": "transcribe_streaming", "signature": "def transcribe_streaming(audio, sample_rate)"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 268, "name": "transcribe", "signature": "def transcribe(audio, sample_rate)"}]}, {"doc": "On a Mac you'll need to set up ffmpeg using: brew install ffmpeg@8 export DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH=\"/opt/homebrew/opt/ffmpeg@8/lib:$DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH\"", "id": "scripts/eval-model-accuracy.py", "kind": "module", "label": "eval-model-accuracy.py", "language": "py", "sha256": "71c5394ac0bd7a9c", "symbol_count": 0, "symbols": []}, {"id": "scripts/eval-speaker-id.py", "kind": "module", "label": "eval-speaker-id.py", "language": "py", "sha256": "d3b8a92df716ae57", "symbol_count": 0, "symbols": []}, {"doc": "Export a decoder_with_attention model for word-level timestamps.  Takes the original decoder_model_merged.ort, adds cross-attention weight outputs by wiring the internal encoder_attn Softmax nodes to new graph outputs, and saves the result as decoder_with_attention.ort.  The modified model is identical to the original — same weights, same computation, same speed — just with 6 additional outputs (one per decoder layer) that surface the attention weights already being computed internally. See the License for the specific language governing permissions and limitations under the License.", "id": "scripts/export_zipvoice_voices_for_cpp.py", "kind": "module", "label": "export_zipvoice_voices_for_cpp.py", "language": "py", "sha256": "968f7d258c3bceb7", "symbol_count": 10, "symbols": [{"doc": "``voice_000_american_female`` -> ``american_female``.", "kind": "function", "line": 55, "name": "slug_from_voice_id", "signature": "def slug_from_voice_id(voice_id)"}, {"doc": "One masculine + one feminine speaker per accent (first of each in file order).", "kind": "function", "line": 60, "name": "select_voices", "signature": "def select_voices(voices)"}, {"doc": "End index (<= max_samples) that ends at a *strong* natural pause when possible.\n\nA hard cut at exactly 4 s often lands mid-word, and ZipVoice then \"continues\" the reference clip\nat the start of the generated speech (audible leakage). Even cutting at a weak inter-word gap can\nleave the clip ending on a dangling function word (e.g. \"...slabs of\"), which also leaks. So we\nprefer the last *phrase-level* pause (comma / sentence boundary, >= ~220 ms of silence), falling\nback to any short pause, then to a hard cut with a fade-out.", "kind": "function", "line": 81, "name": "_clean_cut_index", "signature": "def _clean_cut_index(wav, sr, max_samples)"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 127, "name": "load_clip_pcm16", "signature": "def load_clip_pcm16(path)"}, {"doc": "Transcribes the *exact* embedded clip with Moonshine ASR.\n\nZipVoice needs the clone transcript to match the reference audio; since clips are trimmed to a fixed\n4 seconds, the original VCTK sentence no longer corresponds to what is actually spoken. Transcribing\nthe trimmed clip (like ZipVoice's own auto-transcription) keeps them aligned and avoids reference-clip leakage.", "kind": "class", "line": 146, "name": "_CloneTranscriber", "signature": "class _CloneTranscriber"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 177, "name": "c_escape", "signature": "def c_escape(s)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 181, "name": "main", "signature": "def main()"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 154, "name": "__init__", "signature": "def __init__(self)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 165, "name": "transcribe_pcm16", "signature": "def transcribe_pcm16(self, pcm)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 170, "name": "close", "signature": "def close(self)"}]}, {"doc": "Format (default) or check (--check) the first-party C++ in core/ against the repo's Google-based .clang-format. Vendored/third-party trees are never touched. Runs anywhere clang-format is installed (e.g. `brew install clang-format` on macOS); no Linux or full build required.  Usage: scripts/format-core.sh            # format in place scripts/format-core.sh --check    # non-zero exit if anything is unformatted  Override the binary with CLANG_FORMAT=/path/to/clang-format.", "id": "scripts/format-core.sh", "kind": "module", "label": "format-core.sh", "language": "sh", "sha256": "66ce9d03f3ce0910", "symbol_count": 0, "symbols": []}, {"doc": "Copyright 2026 Moonshine AI (MIT License)", "id": "scripts/generate-diarization-test-audio.py", "kind": "module", "label": "generate-diarization-test-audio.py", "language": "py", "sha256": "5a946787609965a9", "symbol_count": 4, "symbols": [{"kind": "function", "line": 60, "name": "_synthesize_utterance", "signature": "def _synthesize_utterance(voice, text, asset_root)"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 78, "name": "_append_silence", "signature": "def _append_silence(samples, sample_rate, seconds)"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 84, "name": "generate_dialogue_wav", "signature": "def generate_dialogue_wav(asset_root)"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 97, "name": "main", "signature": "def main()"}]}, {"doc": "Regenerate core/silero-vad-model-data.h from the Silero VAD model.  The Silero VAD ships from upstream as an ONNX protobuf. This script converts it to the ONNX Runtime `.ort` flatbuffer format and bakes the bytes into the C header that gets embedded in libmoonshine. The `.ort` format is what every other model in this repo uses: it is smaller, loads faster, works with minimal/mobile ORT builds, and (because ORT can parse it in place) avoids the protobuf alignment reads that fault on 32-bit ARM.  The generated array keeps the historical symbol names (`silero_vad_onnx` / `silero_vad_onnx_len`) so no C++ consumer needs to change; ORT's CreateSessionFromArray auto-detects the format from the bytes.  By default the source .onnx is downloaded from a commit-pinned upstream URL into a temporary directory and checked against a known SHA-256, so nothing is left behind in the tree. Pass --onnx to convert a local model instead.  Note: the .onnx -> .ort conversion is NOT byte-reproducible (ORT embeds non-deterministic data), so regenerating produces a different byte array even from the identical source model. The output is functionally identical; the integrity guarantee is on the source .onnx (SHA-256), not the converted bytes.  Optimization level (`--optimization`) is a space/latency tradeoff, and note that for .ort models ORT applies whatever optimizations are baked in here -- the runtime graph_optimization_level does NOT re-optimize a .ort graph: * disable  -- raw graph, smallest (~onnx size). Constant folding is skipped, so the STFT basis tables are recomputed each inference (slightly slower). No version bump and no tag: the release branch is the mutable source of truth, and build-all-platforms.sh refreshes the v<version> tag from the branch HEAD on its next run.  Usage: scripts/patch-release.sh <commit-ish> [<commit-ish> ...]  Example (fix already committed on main as abc1234): scripts/patch-release.sh abc1234  What it does: 1. Finds the newest release-v* branch (the release you're building). 2. Checks it out at origin's HEAD. 3. Cherry-picks the commits you name onto it. 4. Pushes the branch and returns you to main.  Afterwards re-run: scripts/build-all-platforms.sh It resumes (skipping completed stages) and the remaining stages pick up the new branch HEAD.  IMPORTANT: this is for a release that is still in progress. To ship a fix for a version that is ALREADY fully published, cut a NEW version with scripts/prepare-release.sh instead -- package registries reject re-uploading an existing version.", "id": "scripts/patch-release.sh", "kind": "module", "label": "patch-release.sh", "language": "sh", "sha256": "c211899532edcb62", "symbol_count": 1, "symbols": [{"kind": "function", "line": 32, "name": "main"}]}, {"doc": "============================================================================= Making a Release =============================================================================  A release lives on a per-release branch, release-v<version>, and every build/checkout step tracks that branch's HEAD. You never move tags or force-push by hand: build-all-platforms.sh derives and refreshes the v<version> tag from the branch automatically (the tag exists only because GitHub Releases and SwiftPM need one). So folding a fix into an in-progress release is just \"add a commit to the branch and re-run the build\".  1. Cut the release: scripts/prepare-release.sh 0.0.69 Creates branch release-v0.0.69 off origin/main, rewrites every version string via update-version.sh, commits, and pushes the branch. No tag is created here; you are dropped back on main so you can keep working.  2. Build and publish: scripts/build-all-platforms.sh Builds the newest release-v* branch (override with RELEASE_REF). The local platforms build in an isolated worktree at the branch HEAD; each remote host resets to the same branch HEAD. It is resumable: completed stages are skipped on re-run. build-all refreshes the v<version> tag to the branch HEAD so the publish steps / GitHub Releases have a tag.  3. Normally invoked by scripts/reliability.sh over SSH, but can be run directly on the box from the repo root.  Steps (each contributes to the final pass/fail): 1. Configure + build core with -DMOONSHINE_RELIABILITY=ON (ASan/UBSan) using clang, exporting compile_commands.json. 2. Run the core test suite under the sanitizers. 3. ThreadSanitizer: build the threaded tests into a separate build dir with -DMOONSHINE_SANITIZER=thread and run them (advisory unless TSAN_STRICT=1). 4. Run clang-tidy on first-party sources and fail on any finding that is NOT already recorded in core/.clang-tidy-baseline (i.e. newly introduced). 5. Fuzz each per-module target for FUZZ_SECONDS, saving any crash reproducers.  Environment: FUZZ_SECONDS   seconds per fuzz target (default 900) TIDY_UPDATE_BASELINE  1 => regenerate core/.clang-tidy-baseline from this run instead of gating against it (commit the result). Never fails the run. Default 0. TSAN           1 => run the ThreadSanitizer stage (default 1); 0 to skip TSAN_STRICT    1 => TSan findings fail the run (default 0, advisory) TSAN_TEST_TIMEOUT  per-TSan-test wall-clock limit in seconds (default 600); a timeout is always a hard failure so a hang can't stall the pipeline for hours STREAM_MEMORY_TEST_TIMEOUT  wall-clock limit for transcriber-streaming- memory-test (default 900) MOONSHINE_STREAM_MEMORY_AUDIO_SECONDS  audio seconds fed by that test (default 120); forwarded to the test binary", "id": "scripts/reliability-remote.sh", "kind": "module", "label": "reliability-remote.sh", "language": "sh", "sha256": "379c57b144452afd", "symbol_count": 4, "symbols": [{"kind": "function", "line": 69, "name": "record_failure"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 89, "name": "require_tool"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 183, "name": "run_test"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 439, "name": "run_fuzzer"}]}, {"doc": "Periodic reliability driver. Run this from the Mac (or any dev machine). It:  1. Runs the fast, local static checks (formatting + banned constructs). 2. Syncs the working tree to a native Linux x86 box over SSH (so even uncommitted changes are exercised), preserving the box's large model / test assets. 3. Runs scripts/reliability-remote.sh there (ASan/UBSan build + test suite, clang-tidy, a ThreadSanitizer rebuild + threaded tests, a long-stream memory regression test, and time-boxed per-module fuzzing). 4. Copies logs and any crash reproducers back to core/reliability/artifacts.  The whole run is designed to finish within a few hours (tune FUZZ_SECONDS).  Usage: scripts/reliability.sh  Environment: RELIABILITY_HOST   SSH host of the Linux x86 box (default: petes-alienware-pc) REMOTE_DIR         repo path on that box, relative to $HOME (default: moonshine) FUZZ_SECONDS       seconds per fuzz target (default 900 => ~1h of fuzzing) TIDY_UPDATE_BASELINE 1 => regenerate core/.clang-tidy-baseline from this run (copied back locally to commit) instead of gating on it TSAN               1 => run the ThreadSanitizer stage (default 1); 0 to skip TSAN_STRICT        1 => TSan findings fail the run (default 0, advisory)  The local static checks (banned constructs + formatting) are hard gates: any failure aborts the run before syncing, so drift is never silently skipped. Run scripts/format-core.sh to fix formatting drift wholesale.", "id": "scripts/reliability.sh", "kind": "module", "label": "reliability.sh", "language": "sh", "sha256": "135956af9f059155", "symbol_count": 0, "symbols": []}, {"doc": "Benchmark to compare Moonshine and Whisper model latency in live speech scenarios.  This is an opinionated benchmark that looks at the latency and total compute cost of the two families of models in a situation that is representative of many common real-time voice applications' requirements:  - Speech needs to be responded to as quickly as possible once a user completes a phrase. - The phrases are of durations between a range of one to ten seconds.  These are very different requirements from bulk offline processing scenarios, where the overall throughput of the system is more important, and so the latency on a single segment of speech is less important than the overall throughput of the system. This allows optimizations like batch processing.  We are not claiming that Whisper is not a great model for offline processing, but we do want to highlight the advantages we that Moonshine offers for live speech applications with real-time latency requirements.  The experimental setup is as follows:  - We use the two_cities.wav audio file as a test case, since it has a mix of short and long phrases. You can vary this by passing in your own audio file with the --wav_path argument. - We use the Moonshine Tiny, Base, Tiny Streaming, Small Streaming, and Medium Streaming models. - We compare these to the Whisper Tiny, Base, Small, and Large v3 models. Since the Moonshine Medium Streaming model achieves lower WER than Whisper Large v3 we compare those two, otherwise we compare each with their namesake. - We use the Moonshine VAD segmenter to split the audio into phrases, and feed each phrase to Whisper for transcription.", "id": "scripts/run-benchmarks.py", "kind": "module", "label": "run-benchmarks.py", "language": "py", "sha256": "2d4afeeeb65c12fa", "symbol_count": 3, "symbols": [{"kind": "class", "line": 132, "name": "WhisperListener", "signature": "class WhisperListener(TranscriptEventListener)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 133, "name": "__init__", "signature": "def __init__(self)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 137, "name": "on_line_completed", "signature": "def on_line_completed(self, event)"}]}, {"doc": "One-time setup of the Android toolchain needed to run the moonshine-voice instrumentation tests (scripts/test-android.sh) on an x86_64 Linux host with KVM. Everything installs under $HOME (no sudo), EXCEPT KVM group membership, which must be granted separately once:  sudo usermod -aG kvm \"$USER\"   # then log out/in (or reboot)  Installs: Temurin JDK 17, Android command-line tools, platform-tools, emulator, the compileSdk platform + build-tools, the NDK + CMake pinned by build.gradle.kts, an x86_64 system image, and an AVD for it.", "id": "scripts/setup-android-ci.sh", "kind": "module", "label": "setup-android-ci.sh", "language": "sh", "sha256": "af64be2490cf0782", "symbol_count": 1, "symbols": [{"kind": "function", "line": 27, "name": "log"}]}, {"doc": "Run the moonshine-voice Android library's instrumentation tests on a real device or emulator (./gradlew connectedAndroidTest). Unlike scripts/build- android.sh (which only builds the AAR) and scripts/test-examples.sh (which only compiles the example apps), this actually installs and runs the library on an Android runtime, so it is the real validation of the library on a device: a successful link does not prove the bundled ONNX Runtime's symbols resolve on an older OS, but running the tests on a matching-API emulator does. The library's minSdk comes from build.gradle.kts; boot an emulator at (or above) that API to exercise the supported floor.  Usage: ./scripts/test-android.sh [--avd NAME] [--serial SERIAL]  Options: --avd NAME      Boot this AVD headless, wait for it, run the tests, then shut it down on exit. Without --avd, a device/emulator must already be connected (see --serial). --serial SERIAL Target a specific adb device/emulator serial.  Environment: ANDROID_HOME or ANDROID_SDK_ROOT — required.  ABI note: the library ships native libs for arm64-v8a, armeabi-v7a and x86_64 (see build.gradle.kts abiFilters), so the device/emulator's ABI must be one of those. On Apple Silicon use an \"arm64-v8a\" system image; x86_64 emulators only run on an x86_64 host. Apple Silicon cannot run armeabi-v7a (32-bit ARM) emulators; test that ABI on a real 32-bit-capable device via --serial.", "id": "scripts/test-android.sh", "kind": "module", "label": "test-android.sh", "language": "sh", "sha256": "900b86ce6463ac57", "symbol_count": 3, "symbols": [{"kind": "function", "line": 37, "name": "log"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 38, "name": "die"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 82, "name": "cleanup"}]}, {"id": "scripts/test-core.sh", "kind": "module", "label": "test-core.sh", "language": "sh", "sha256": "5dd8c7744c618a4e", "symbol_count": 0, "symbols": []}, {"doc": "Tests that the code in the documentation still works, by executing the fenced code blocks in README.md and python/README.md (see python/tests/test_docs.py) and running the getting-started notebook end to end, all against a freshly built wheel. Usage: ./scripts/test-examples.sh [--repo OWNER/REPO] [--tag vX.Y.Z] [--workdir DIR] [--keep-workdir] ./scripts/test-examples.sh --local-examples [--workdir DIR] [--keep-workdir] ./scripts/test-examples.sh --local-library [--workdir DIR]  With --local-examples, skips GitHub downloads and copies this repository's examples/android and examples/ios into a temp tree (same layout as extracted release archives), then runs the same Gradle / xcodebuild checks.  With --local-library (implies --local-examples), the examples are built against THIS checkout's library instead of the published artifacts, so you can verify a library change (e.g. a new API or a lowered minSdk) before publishing: - Android: builds + installs the AAR into the local Maven cache (via scripts/build-android.sh local), injects mavenLocal() as the first repository (via a Gradle init script) so it takes precedence, and syncs each example's requested moonshine-voice version to this checkout's coordinates(). Requires swift/Moonshine.xcframework to exist; when it is missing, scripts/build-swift.sh is run to build it first. For a strategically sampled set of configurations (one per code path, biased toward the smallest model that exercises it), this script: 1. asks the C API (via moonshine-download-smoke) for the download manifest, 2. downloads every listed file into a fresh temp directory with curl, 3. loads the corresponding engine from that directory and runs one trivial inference.  whole point: this verifies the catalog lists everything each model needs.  After the native samples, it also drives the framework-level download tests that exercise the real AssetDownloader on each platform (they are opt-in and skip on a plain `swift test` / `connectedAndroidTest`): - Swift: MOONSHINE_DOWNLOAD_TESTS=1 swift test --filter AssetDownloaderNetworkTests (macOS, when `swift` and swift/Moonshine.xcframework are present). - Android: connectedAndroidTest for AssetDownloaderTest with moonshineDownloadTests=1 (only when a device/emulator is already connected; this script never boots one - use scripts/test-android.sh for emulator lifecycle).  This test hits the network, so it is intentionally NOT part of the hermetic scripts/test-core.sh. Run it directly (it assumes a fast connection) or from scripts/build-all-platforms.sh / CI. Usage: ./scripts/test-python.sh                Build the wheel first, then test. ./scripts/test-python.sh --skip-build   Reuse the wheel already in python/dist/ (faster iteration).", "id": "scripts/test-python.sh", "kind": "module", "label": "test-python.sh", "language": "sh", "sha256": "0f321c5816eb5534", "symbol_count": 1, "symbols": [{"kind": "function", "line": 28, "name": "cleanup"}]}, {"doc": "Evaluate TTS intelligibility: Moonshine synthesis (Kokoro / Piper vocoders) vs Whisper large-v3 transcripts.  Ground-truth lines come from ``scripts/data/wiki-text/<language_tag>.txt`` (default), a sectioned ``wiki-text.txt`` file (``[en_us]`` / ``[de_de]`` sections), or any path you pass to ``--wiki-text``.  By default the script downloads **WikiText-2** (``wikitext-2-raw-v1``) for English locales (``en_us``, ``en_gb``). Other Moonshine TTS languages use the same line-cleaning heuristics on **Wikimedia Wikipedia** snapshots (``wikimedia/wikipedia``, config ``20231101.<lang>``), because WikiText-2 is English-only on Hugging Face.  For **German** (``de`` / ``de_de``), Wikipedia sampling **ranks** paragraph candidates toward narrative prose: corporate and regulatory leads (GmbH, Verordnung, “steht für …”, many initialisms) get a lower priority than story-like lines. Delete ``scripts/data/wiki-text/de_de.txt`` (or ``de.txt``) to re-download after changing this logic.  With no arguments, the script evaluates **all** TTS languages from the native catalog, refreshes per-language ``wiki-text/*.txt`` from Hugging Face (unless ``--no-wiki-download``), scores **10 lines** per language by default (override with ``--max-lines-per-lang``), and writes JSON to ``scripts/data/tts_g2p_intelligibility_report.json``. Synthesized audio for each track is cached as 16-bit mono ``.wav`` files under ``scripts/data/tts_g2p_intelligibility_wav_cache/`` (see ``--tts-wav-cache-dir`` / ``--no-tts-wav-cache``) so reruns skip Kokoro/Piper/Moonshine resynthesis; Whisper transcription still runs every time. Pass ``--no-cache`` to always resynthesize while still writing cache files (read is skipped). Cache files live under ``<cache-dir>/<lang>/<first-two-chars-of-stem>/`` with basenames ``<first-12-chars-of-line>_<engine>_<sha256>.wav`` (engines: ``moonshine``, ``kokoro``, ``piper``).  By default, ``--tts-root`` points at ``core/moonshine-tts/data``; after voice assets are downloaded, files from ``<tts-root>/<language_tag>/`` (e.g. ``ru/dict.tsv``) are copied over the cache so G2P", #### `main_i2s_audio_test.cc`
**Path:** `micro/examples/rp2350/src/main_i2s_audio_test.cc`
**File Doc:** *Standalone speaker / audio-output bring-up test (the `moonshine_micro_i2s_audio_test` target). It proves the I2S amp + speaker are wired up and making sound, driven by the same I2sAudioOutput backend the live apps use. Besides tones and recorded clips it also runs the neural TTS engine (the same one the live apps speak with) so the whole render path is exercised -- it does NOT touch the VAD/STT capture pipeline.  Designed for the Adafruit MAX98357A I2S class-D amp (#3006, https://www.adafruit.com/product/3006), which has its own I2S DAC -- so unlike the old PWM speaker there is no carrier and no RC reconstruction filter. Connect your own 4-8 ohm speaker to the amp's screw terminals.  Wiring (see src/i2s_out.pio; LRC = BCLK + 1 for the sideset pair):  Vin  -> Pico VSYS   (physical pin 39)   ; 2.5-5.5 V; use VSYS not VBUS GND  -> Pico GND    (physical pin 38) DIN  -> GP10        (physical pin 14)   ; I2S data BCLK -> GP11        (physical pin 15)   ; bit clock LRC  -> GP12        (physical pin 16)   ; word select (LRCLK) GAIN -> (leave open -> 9 dB)   SD -> (leave open -> enabled, (L+R)/2 mono)  GP10/11/12 are chosen so they don't collide with the I2S mic test (GP0/1/2). What you should hear: a rising A-major arpeggio, then a tone sweep, then 1 s recordings of "a", "b", "c", then the neural TTS voice saying the letters "a"/"b"/"c" and the words "hello"/"wifi", looping.*

#### `main_i2s_relay.cc`
**Path:** `micro/examples/rp2350/src/main_i2s_relay.cc`
**File Doc:** *Dumb PCM -> I2S relay (the `moonshine_micro_i2s_relay` target).  This firmware does NO synthesis, VAD or STT. It is the device half of the hardware-in-the-loop TTS eval harness (scripts/hw_tts_eval/): the laptop synthesizes speech, streams the raw PCM here over USB CDC, and this app plays it out the MAX98357A I2S amp so an external mic can record the real acoustic path. Keeping the device dumb means the loop measures the exact same I2sAudioOutput path the live apps use, with nothing else in the way.  Wiring (identical to moonshine_micro_i2s_audio_test; see src/i2s_out.pio): Vin  -> Pico VSYS (pin 39)   GND -> GND DIN  -> GP10   BCLK -> GP11   LRC -> GP12   (MAX98357A / Adafruit 3006) GAIN -> open (9 dB)   SD -> open (enabled, (L+R)/2 mono)  Protocol (line commands over CDC; binary PCM is framed, not line-based): PING              -> replies "PONG" PLAY <rate> <n>   -> then read `n` int16 LE samples, streamed in hops of up to kHop samples, each hop prefixed by the 0xA5 0x5A sync (mirrors usb_audio_io.cc). Samples are written to I2sAudioOutput at <rate> Hz. When done, replies "PLAYED <m>" with the number of samples actually played (m == n on a clean stream).  PICO_STDIO_DEFAULT_CRLF=0 (see CMakeLists.txt) keeps 0x0A/0x0D PCM bytes from being mangled on the way in, and keeps our text replies from getting CR injected on the way out.*

**Functions:**
- `ReadLine` (line 71) `int ReadLine(char* buf, int maxlen)` - *Read one newline-terminated line into `buf` (NUL-terminated), blocking until a non-empty line arrives. Feeds the watchdog each idle slice. CR and LF both terminate; blank lines are skipped.*
- `ReadByteTimed` (line 88) `int ReadByteTimed(int timeout_ms)` - *Read one byte, waiting up to ~timeout_ms. Returns -1 on timeout.*
- `ReadHop` (line 98) `int ReadHop(int16_t* out, int n)` - *Scan for the 0xA5 0x5A sync, then read up to `n` int16 LE samples into `out`. Returns the number of samples read; a short return means the host stalled mid-hop (each sample byte read times out so a dropped frame can't wedge the device -- see the deadlock note in usb_audio_io.cc). Returns -1 if no sync arrives within ~2 s (host aborted the stream).*
- `PlayStream` (line 140) `int PlayStream(spelling::I2sAudioOutput& out, int rate, int total)` - *Receive `total` samples from the host into RAM, then play them to the I2S amp at `rate` Hz. Returns the number of samples played.  Why buffer the whole clip instead of streaming hop->FIFO directly: the PIO I2S TX FIFO is only a few frames deep, and reading a 512-sample hop over USB CDC (one getchar per byte) takes far longer than those few frames play out. A read-then-write loop therefore underruns the FIFO on every hop boundary -- the SM stalls mid-stream and the amp clicks, which sounds like continuous broadband static. Receiving the whole clip first (no real-time constraint; USB flow-control backpressures the host) then streaming RAM->FIFO keeps the FIFO fed faster than real time, so playback is glitch-free.*

#### `log_mel.cc`
**Path:** `micro/feature-generation/src/log_mel.cc`
**File Doc:** *Heap-free log-mel spectrogram for the on-device build.  Reflect-pad (center=True), windowed STFT, squared-magnitude, Slaney mel filterbank, crop to target_frames, log(value + eps), per-clip mean/std normalisation with std clamped >= 1e-3.  The DIFFERENCES from the desktop port are all about memory:  1. Compute() takes a caller-supplied output buffer instead of returning std::vector. Saves 64 KB of heap traffic per call.  2. Reflect padding is done on-the-fly per sample inside the framing loop. The desktop port materialised a 16512-sample `padded` vector (~66 KB).  3. STFT + power-spectrum + filterbank multiply are FUSED into a single pass: for each output frame we compute one 257-bin power row on the stack, then immediately scatter it through the mel filterbank into one column of the output buffer. The desktop port allocated a full (n_freq, n_frames) power matrix (~200 KB) and a (n_mels, n_frames) mel matrix (~64 KB).  4. log() and normalisation run in-place on the output buffer. Saves another 64 KB.  With our defaults this drops peak per-call heap usage from ~450 KB to 0 (just ~5 KB on the stack for frame_buf, spectrum, and one power row). The window + filterbank still live as heap std::vector members of LogMelSpectrogram itself (84 KB total), allocated ONCE in the constructor.*

**Functions:**
- `ReflectIndex` (line 69) `inline int ReflectIndex(int i, int n)` - *Reflect index without duplicating the boundary. Matches torch.nn.functional.pad(x, (pad, pad), mode="reflect"): index -1 -> 1, -2 -> 2, ..., and on the right side, n -> n-2, n+1 -> n-3, ...  `n` is the original waveform length, `i` is the padded-coords index in [-pad, n + pad). The implementation handles only the edge regions: callers in the hot loop pass already-validated indices in [0, n) directly past this helper. We use it from the framing loop where we sometimes step a sample or two past either edge due to center padding.*

#### `tts_cli.cc`
**Path:** `micro/neural-tts/host/tts_cli.cc`
**File Doc:** *Native (desktop) driver for the on-device neural TTS engine.  Runs the EXACT C++ pipeline the RP2350 firmware runs -- shared g2p front end -> Klatt rule durations -> diphone/word unit selection -> int8 RVQ decode through the s16x8 TFLM graph -> WORLD-lite vocoder -- but on the host, using the portable TFLM reference kernels (see host/tflm_ref/) instead of CMSIS-NN. The flash pack is loaded from a .bin file rather than linked from flash.  This is the fast, flash-free equivalent of the `moonshine_micro_tts` firmware + tts_speak.py: same bytes in, same PCM out, no board required.  Usage: tts_cli "hello there" -o out.wav tts_cli --ipa "h@loU" -o hi.wav tts_cli --pack path/to/neural_tts_pack.bin "text" -o out.wav tts_cli "text" -o -            # raw int16 LE PCM to stdout*

#### `neural_tts.cc`
**Path:** `micro/neural-tts/src/neural_tts.cc`
**File Doc:** *Black-box neural TTS pipeline (see neural_tts.h). Port of the host reference scripts/synth_diphone_world.py synthesize() with the shipping flag set; every stage is annotated with its Python counterpart.  Arena life cycle per chunk (all caller arena; the G2P front end's small std::string/vector transients are the only malloc heap use):  [plan: runs, D, parts, candidate sets, track, f0]   -- whole chunk [decode: PbDecoder (+TFLM arena), one-unit cache]   -- rolled back [render: WorldLiteSynth + kissfft plans in arena]    -- reuses decode's  The control track is materialized in the decoder's *quantized log domain* (int16, output_scale, benv as log10-amplitude): all assembly math (crossfades, gain EQ, timbre/energy offsets, declination) is additive there, and frames convert to linear WorldFrames only at the vocoder boundary.*

#### `tflm_host_stub.cc`
**Path:** `micro/test-support/host/tflm_host_stub.cc`
**File Doc:** *Host (desktop) implementations of the handful of TFLM platform hooks that the modules and the micro_test.h harness reference: the MicroPrintf logging family and tflite::InitializeTarget().  The vendored pico-tflmicro provides these for the RP2350 via system_setup.cpp / debug_log.cpp, both of which call into the Pico SDK and therefore cannot be compiled on the host. For the pure-logic unit tests (feature-generation, the VAD segmenter, the STT predictor, the TTS G2P) we don't need the interpreter at all -- only logging and a no-op init -- so this tiny shim lets those tests build and run on a laptop with a normal compiler.  Interpreter-level tests (real MicroInterpreter inference) are built for the RP2350 target instead, where the full pico-tflmicro library is available.*

#### `moonshine-download-smoke.cpp`
**Path:** `core/moonshine-download-smoke.cpp`
**File Doc:** *moonshine-download-smoke: a tiny CLI used by scripts/test-model-downloads.sh to verify that the native download manifests are complete. It has two modes:  moonshine-download-smoke manifest <modality> [spec...] Prints one "<url>\t<relative_path>" line per required file, resolved from the C API dependency functions (the single source of truth). The bash harness downloads each url into <root>/<relative_path>.  moonshine-download-smoke run <modality> <root> [spec...] Loads the engine from the freshly downloaded <root> and runs one trivial inference, exiting 0 on success. If a required file was missing from the manifest, loading or inference fails here - which is exactly what this test is meant to catch.  Modalities and their [spec...] arguments: stt    <language> [<model_arch>] intent <model_name> <variant> tts    <language> <voice> g2p    <language>  HTTP lives entirely in the bash harness (curl); this tool never touches the network. It only resolves manifests and exercises the on-disk load path.*

#### `zipvoice-custom-ops.cpp`
**Path:** `core/moonshine-tts/src/zipvoice-custom-ops.cpp`
**File Doc:** *Custom ONNX Runtime operators for the ZipVoice Zipformer (domain ai.zipvoice).  Ported from the standalone ``custom_ops/swoosh_op.cc`` in the ZipVoice repo. The only structural change is that these kernels are compiled *into* libmoonshine (which already links onnxruntime) and registered on a session directly via ``zipvoice_register_custom_ops`` rather than being built as a separate shared library that ORT ``dlopen``s at runtime. This avoids loading a .so/.dll, which some platforms (e.g. iOS) make difficult.  SwooshL / SwooshR: the Zipformer activations. Exported to ONNX they decompose into ~11 element-wise nodes each; these ops collapse each activation into a single kernel. softplus(z) = log(1 + exp(z)) = max(z, 0) + log1p(exp(-|z|)) SwooshL(x)  = softplus(x - 4.0) - 0.08 * x - 0.035 SwooshR(x)  = softplus(x - 1.0) - 0.08 * x - 0.313261687 GluGate: out[..., c] = x[..., c] * sigmoid(x[..., C + c]),  C = lastdim / 2 DepthwiseConv1d: fuses Transpose -> depthwise Conv1d ('same' pad K//2) -> Transpose in [T,N,C]. BiasNorm: RMS-style norm of (x - bias) over channels, scaled by exp(log_scale). Bypass: per-channel residual lerp src_orig + (src - src_orig) * scale.*

The in-memory BinTokenizer constructor parses an untrusted byte blob (a tokenizer.bin loaded from disk or an app bundle), so it is a natural fuzz target. #### `fuzz-tensor-view.cpp`
**Path:** `core/reliability/fuzz-tensor-view.cpp`
**File Doc:** *libFuzzer harness for MoonshineTensorView construction.  The shape/dtype/data constructor forwards to moonshine_tensor_from_shape_and_dtype, which turns an (attacker-influenced) shape into an element count, a byte size, an allocation, and a memcpy. A crafted shape can overflow the size arithmetic; this harness feeds arbitrary dimensions (including huge values whose product overflows) so ASan/UBSan catch any regression in the overflow handling. Unsupported dtypes throw by design, so construction is wrapped; only sanitizer errors fail the run.*

#### `tts-repeated-memory-test.cpp`
**Path:** `core/tts-repeated-memory-test.cpp`
**File Doc:** *Repeated-use memory regression test for the text-to-speech synthesizers.  The transcriber has a long-stream memory test (transcriber-streaming-memory- test.cpp); this is the TTS analogue. It exercises each available engine (Kokoro, Piper, ZipVoice, English only) through the public C API in two loops that probe the two distinct leak surfaces:  * "synth"  - one synthesizer, many moonshine_text_to_speech() calls (each output buffer freed). Catches leaks in the inference / G2P / per-call allocation path. * "reload" - repeatedly create and free the synthesizer handle. Catches leaks in model load / teardown and the handle table.  TTS exposes no internal retained-byte accessor (unlike the transcriber's stream_vad_completed_audio_bytes), so the signal here is process RSS: the test samples resident memory after every iteration and fails on sustained, post-warmup growth using the same regression heuristic as the transcriber test. onnxruntime arena allocators grow during warmup and then plateau, so the warmup window is skipped and only a persistent upward trend is treated as a regression.  The bundled TTS data (core/moonshine-tts/data) is required. Pass its path as argv[1], or run with a working directory from which it can be discovered (repo root, test-assets/, or core/build). Engines whose assets are absent are skipped. Invoked from scripts/reliability-remote.sh.*

**Functions:**
- `read_rss_kb` (line 54) `size_t read_rss_kb()`
- `median` (line 90) `size_t median(std::vector<size_t> values)`

- `detect_continual_growth` (line 117) `bool detect_continual_growth(const std::vector<size_t> &samples,
                             siz...` - *Mirrors transcriber-streaming-memory-test's detector: fits a line to the post-warmup samples and reports sustained growth only when the median gain, the fraction of non-decreasing steps, and the fitted slope all clear their thresholds. This tolerates one-off jumps and allocator caching while still catching an unbounded per-iteration leak.*

When `advisory` is true a positive finding is logged but does not fail the run (RSS across repeated model load/free is dominated by allocator / OS page retention rather than a reliable leak signal); otherwise it is a hard gate.*

#### `moonshine-model-catalog.h`
**Path:** `core/moonshine-model-catalog.h`
**File Doc:** *Native catalog of downloadable model assets (speech-to-text transcription, the optional alphanumeric spelling model, and intent-recognition embedding models). This is the C++ port of the tables that previously lived only in python/src/moonshine_voice/download.py, promoted here so every language binding resolves the exact same download manifest from a single source of truth. The TTS / G2P dependency catalog lives separately under core/moonshine-tts/ and is surfaced by moonshine_get_tts_dependencies / moonshine_get_g2p_dependencies; this file covers the remaining model types.*

#### `lwipopts.h`
**Path:** `micro/examples/rp2350/lwipopts.h`
**File Doc:** *Minimal lwIP configuration for the voice WiFi-setup app (moonshine_micro_echo_wifi).  This firmware only needs to ASSOCIATE with an AP, obtain a DHCP lease, and read back the assigned IPv4 address -- it never opens a socket. So this is tuned for the smallest possible footprint on the RAM-constrained RP2350, where the SpellingCNN tensor arena already claims the bulk of SRAM: * NO_SYS / poll mode (no RTOS, no threads) -- matches pico_cyw43_arch_lwip_poll. * TCP, DNS, sockets, and the netconn API are all compiled out. * Small pbuf pool / mem heap, since DHCP exchanges only a handful of small UDP datagrams.  If a future revision needs an actual network client (NTP, HTTP, ...), bump MEM_SIZE / PBUF_POOL_SIZE and re-enable LWIP_TCP / LWIP_DNS, and re-check the RAM budget against the arena.   --- Core model: bare-metal, polled (no RTOS) ------------------------------  --- Memory: use lwIP's own pools (not libc malloc), kept small ------------*

#### `audio_service.h`
**Path:** `micro/examples/rp2350/src/audio_service.h`
**File Doc:** *Live USB audio service: turns the laptop into the RP2350's mic + speaker.  The host (examples/rp2350/scripts/usb_audio_bridge.py) captures the laptop mic at 16 kHz and streams it to the device as framed 32 ms hops over USB CDC. The device runs the streaming VAD on those hops; when a speech segment ends it front-aligns the 1 s clip, classifies it with the SpellingCNN, sends the result back, and speaks the recognized letter/digit via the formant TTS, streaming that PCM back to the host to play on the laptop speaker.  VAD (~36 KiB arena), the SpellingCNN classifier (~366 KiB arena) and the TTS synth (arena working memory) never run at the same time, so they reuse the SINGLE tensor arena sequentially (Vad -> Classifier -> StreamSynth -> Vad). `window` is the reused 1 s int16 waveform buffer (g_waveform) that doubles as the sliding capture window and the front-aligned STT clip; no extra big SRAM buffer is allocated. int16 (vs fp32) halves it to 32 KiB; the VAD + STT front-ends convert to float at the read site.*

**Functions:**
- `RecognizerInit` (line 38) `void RecognizerInit(kiss_fftr_state* fft);` - *Build the persistent recognizer front-end (the streaming VAD mel front-end, the STT log-mel, and their shared 512-pt FFT). Call once before RecognizeOne. The heavy front-end objects live in BSS (not the small core stack).*
- `RecognizeOne` (line 46) `int RecognizeOne(AudioInput& input, uint8_t* arena, std::size_t arena_size, int16_t* window, int window_samples, float* out_prob);` - *Listen on `input` until the streaming VAD reports a completed speech segment, front-align the 1 s clip into `window`, classify it with the SpellingCNN, and return the predicted class index (writing the softmax probability to `*out_prob`). Blocks (emitting idle heartbeats) until a clip is recognized. Reuses the shared tensor `arena` for the VAD then the classifier. Emits the same "listening" / "VAD start" / "VAD end" / "RESULT" logs the host expects.*
- `SetTtsVolume` (line 61) `void SetTtsVolume(float volume);` - *Playback volume for the spoken reply, as a linear multiplier on the TTS PCM.  Unlike the microphone input (whose absolute level we can't choose, and which RecognizeOne RMS-normalizes before the STT front-end so the quiet I2S mic clears the log-mel eps floor), the TTS reply is OUR signal: the streaming synth already self-normalizes each utterance to ~-1 dBFS (VoiceParams::output_gain + a soft limiter), so its peak is predictable. That makes "volume" a clean scalar we get to pick: 1.0 plays at full scale (loudest, and cleanest on a small speaker, which needs the whole range to stay above the noise floor); values < 1.0 attenuate. Values > 1.0 are allowed but will clip the already-near-full-scale reply, so prefer <= 1.0. Applied in Speak() on every path (echo / echo_hardware / wifi), so it's the single TTS-loudness knob.*
- `TtsVolume` (line 62) `float TtsVolume();`
- `Speak` (line 68) `void Speak(const char* text, AudioOutput& output, AudioInput& input, uint8_t* arena, std::size_t arena_size);` - *Synthesize `text` with the formant TTS and stream it to `output`, draining `input` while we speak so our own audio (and room echo) can't re-trigger the VAD, then hold a short mute tail. Reuses the tensor `arena` as synth scratch. The PCM is scaled by TtsVolume() (see SetTtsVolume) before output.*
- `RunAudioService` (line 77) `void RunAudioService(AudioInput& input, AudioOutput& output, uint8_t* arena, std::size_t arena_size, kiss_fftr_state* fft, int16_t* window, int window_samples);` - *Never returns: runs the live recognition loop forever. Microphone audio comes from `input`, the spoken reply goes to `output` -- so the same loop runs on host-tethered USB audio or real on-board I2S hardware unchanged. `arena`/ `arena_size` is the shared TFLM tensor arena; `fft` is the shared 512-pt real-FFT state; `window`/`window_samples` is the 1 s fp32 buffer (kClipNumSamples) reused as the sliding capture window and the STT clip.*

**Path:** `micro/examples/rp2350/src/i2s_audio_io.h`
**File Doc:** *I2S microphone input for the on-board echo service (SPH0645 / Adafruit 3421).  Wiring (arduino-pico I2SInput.ino convention): DOUT -> GPIO0   BCLK <- GPIO1   LRCL <- GPIO2   SEL -> GND (left channel)  Capture is DMA-backed: a single DMA channel streams the PIO RX FIFO into a wrap-around ring buffer continuously, so audio is never dropped while the CPU is busy between hops (FFT + VAD inference). ReadHop just copies the next hop of already-captured samples out of the ring; it does not gate the PIO. See i2s_audio_io.cc for the ring sizing and L/R parity details.*
